items.body:
By Maxwell Akalaare Adombila

Ghana’s Environmental Protection Authority has issued a pre-closure notice to Chinese-owned Cardinal Namdini Mining over an alleged unreported accident as it ramps up enforcement across the mining sector, a senior regulator said.

EPA Deputy Chief Executive for Operations Michael Ayamga also told Reuters the authority is reviewing findings from a recent inspection of South African miner Gold Fields’ GFIJ.J Tarkwa operation and shut down Chinese-owned Earl International Group last week over what he described as a legacy compliance issue linked to illegal gold mining activity.

Ayamga added that the authority also fined AngloGold’s AU.N smaller Iduapriem mine last year for environmental breaches that he declined to detail.

Sector Oversight Tightened to Boost Revenue

A spokesperson for Earl said the company had addressed the EPA’s concerns and was cleared to resume operations on Monday, citing an environmental permit signed by the regulator’s chief executive on September 28.

Cardinal Namdini Mining, owned by China’s Shandong Gold, and South African miner AngloGold did not respond immediately to requests for comment.

Ghana, Africa’s biggest gold producer, has tightened oversight of its mining sector to boost revenue, increase local participation and strengthen compliance. The government has also raised royalties, expanded local-content rules and is advancing a new mining law to increase state oversight and Ghanaian ownership of the lucrative sector.

The EPA, meanwhile, is shifting from periodic inspections to continuous monitoring and enforcement, with environmental, social and governance audits planned across the sector, Ayamga said.

“We don’t want to be reactive but proactive,” he said. “We want to move beyond one-off visits and audits to enforcement.”

Gold Fields Inspection Report Under Review

The EPA management recently received a report from its team of inspectors on Gold Fields’ Tarkwa gold operation and is reviewing the findings to determine whether further engagement with the company is needed, Ayamga said.

The EPA has not disclosed any findings from the inspection, a Gold Fields representative said in response to questions.

Gold Fields said it was notified on September 14 of the regulator’s intention to conduct a broad environmental, social, governance and socio-economic impact assessment at Tarkwa.

The miner said it had sought additional time to review the scope of the assessment and obtain advice before determining its position.

Gold Fields added that Tarkwa is subjected to regular monitoring, independent assurance and regulatory oversight. It has maintained ISO 14001 environmental certification for 23 years and International Cyanide Management Code certification for 18 years, the company added.

For Cardinal, Ayamga said the notice partly related to the alleged failure to promptly report a tailings pipeline decoupling, resulting in a spill from a mine-waste transport system.

Gold Fields is seeking to secure the long-term future of Tarkwa, which faces a mining lease expiry in 2027 after losing the smaller Damang mine last year.

items.title: Goolsbee, do Fed: manter inflação alta por tanto tempo é “brincar com fogo”
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente do Federal Reserve de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmou nesta terça-feira que permitir que a inflação permaneça acima da meta do Fed por 5 anos e meio é “brincar com fogo”, observando que o Fed pode precisar responder a um choque de oferta com efeitos de longo prazo.
items.body:
O presidente do Federal Reserve de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmou nesta terça-feira que permitir que a inflação permaneça acima da meta do Fed por 5 anos e meio é “brincar com fogo”, observando que o Fed pode precisar responder a um choque de oferta com efeitos de longo prazo.
“É uma situação desagradável... (mas) acho que temos que considerar a possibilidade de responder a esses choques persistentes”, disse Goolsbee. Ele afirmou ser um dos formuladores de políticas mais otimistas do Fed no que diz respeito às suas expectativas sobre a trajetória das taxas, mas, antes de reduzir as taxas, “precisamos ter alguma evidência de que a inflação está voltando a cair, de que essas situações que deveriam ser temporárias estão, de fato, desaparecendo”.

items.title: Two-time NBA champ J.R. Smith arrested on assault charge
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two-time NBA champion J.R. Smith was arrested on a charge of family violence in Texas on Monday, according to multiple reports.
items.body:
Two-time NBA champion J.R. Smith was arrested on a charge of family violence in Texas on Monday, according to multiple reports.
No bond had been set and Smith, 41, remained behind bars at the Hunt County Detention Center as of midday on Tuesday, according to jail records.
Smith was arrested by the Royse City Police Department on a warrant issued by the Southlake Police Department for a charge of assault causing bodily injury family violence. Police did not release any further details.
Smith was arrested by the Royse City Police Department on a warrant issued by police in Southlake, Texas, for a charge of family violence assault causing bodily injury. Police did not release any further details.
Smith, a 6-foot-6 shooting guard, won NBA championships with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2015-16) and Los Angeles Lakers (2019-20) during a 16-year career with five teams.
The 2012-13 Sixth Man of the Year averaged 12.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 977 career games (395 starts) with the New Orleans Hornets, Denver Nuggets, New York Knicks, Cavaliers and Lakers. The Hornets drafted him in the first round (18th overall) in 2004.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Williams no ve urgencia para próxima alza de tasas de la Fed
items.author: Michael Derby
items.creator: Michael Derby
items.summary: El presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmó el martes que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para analizar los datos antes de decidir cuándo volver a subir las tasas, y señaló que es probable que se produzca un alza más antes de que termine el año.
items.body:
El presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmó el martes que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para analizar los datos antes de decidir cuándo volver a subir las tasas, y señaló que es probable que se produzca un alza más antes de que termine el año.
"Con las medidas de política monetaria que adoptamos en nuestra reunión de septiembre, no hay necesidad de actuar con urgencia", afirmó Williams en la Universidad de Buffalo, en Nueva York.
Analizar los datos que vayan llegando antes de decidir los próximos pasos "debería aportar mayor claridad" sobre el comportamiento de la economía, señaló Williams.
"Si la economía evoluciona de una manera que se ajuste en líneas generales a mi previsión, podría ser adecuado realizar un nuevo ajuste al alza del rango objetivo de los fondos federales a finales de este año para favorecer un retorno más oportuno de la inflación al objetivo", señaló Williams.
El funcionario añadió que "ésa es solo mi previsión, y el tiempo —y el conjunto de los datos— lo dirán".
Los comentarios de Williams sobre las perspectivas de las tasas se producen en un momento en que los mercados financieros están descontando que la Fed dé continuidad a la subida de tasas de septiembre, que elevó el rango objetivo en un cuarto de punto porcentual a 3,75%-4%.
Los mercados de futuros ven muchas posibilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas en su reunión de octubre, una idea a la que Williams pareció oponerse.
Williams señaló que, dado el sólido crecimiento de la economía y la estabilidad del mercado laboral, las presiones sobre los precios pueden ser ahora el principal foco de atención de la política monetaria.
"Es imperativo que volvamos a situar la inflación en nuestro objetivo del 2% de forma sostenida", afirmó. "Para ello, debemos asegurarnos de que las perturbaciones inflacionarias adversas no se afiancen y de que cualquier efecto de segunda ronda sobre la inflación siga siendo moderado".
La Fed está subiendo las tasas para hacer frente a las presiones que llevan más de media década superando el objetivo de inflación del 2%.
Dichas presiones se han agravado este año debido a los aranceles comerciales del presidente Donald Trump y al aumento de los precios de la energía vinculado a la guerra en Oriente Medio.
A los responsables de la Fed les preocupa cada vez más que la inflación no vuelva al objetivo a tiempo y que sea necesario tomar medidas para garantizar que la población no acabe aceptando como normal una inflación persistentemente alta.
Williams señaló que la inversión en inteligencia artificial también está contribuyendo a aumentar las presiones sobre los precios, al tiempo que añadió que las presiones relacionadas con los aranceles se han atenuado en gran medida.
Williams afirmó que prevé que la inflación cierre el año en torno al 3,5%, ya que las presiones sobre los precios se moderarán el próximo año, en el camino hacia el retorno de la inflación al objetivo fijado para 2028.

items.title: Red Sox return LHP Garrett Crochet from IL for wild-card round
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Boston Red Sox reinstated left-hander Garrett Crochet from the 60-day injured list after recovering from left shoulder inflammation as the team gets set to face the rival New York Yankees on Tuesday in an American League wild-card series.
items.body:
The Boston Red Sox reinstated left-hander Garrett Crochet from the 60-day injured list after recovering from left shoulder inflammation as the team gets set to face the rival New York Yankees on Tuesday in an American League wild-card series.
Crochet, 27, made just six starts this season and has not pitched in a major league game since April 25 against the Baltimore Orioles. He was 3-3 with a 6.30 ERA to open the first month of the season.
A two-time All-Star who finished second in American League Cy Young Award voting last season, Crochet did not make a minor league rehab appearance this season but has thrown bullpen sessions, as well as live batting practice, as part of his recovery.
To make room on the 40-man roster, right-hander Justin Slaten was transferred to the 60-day injured list with a right elbow injury.
Crochet is expected to be used out of the bullpen by the Red Sox in the current series, although he has not pitched in relief since 2023 when he made 13 appearances for the Chicago White Sox in his return from Tommy John surgery.
In six major league seasons, Crochet is 30-27 with a 3.17 ERA in 142 appearances (70 starts) for the White Sox (2020-24) and Red Sox.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Athletics' Zack Gelof sues over injury at Detroit's Comerica Park
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Zack Gelof of the Athletics is suing the Detroit Tigers, alleging that a July knee injury was caused by sliding into an exposed metal fence at Comerica Park.
items.body:
Zack Gelof of the Athletics is suing the Detroit Tigers, alleging that a July knee injury was caused by sliding into an exposed metal fence at Comerica Park.
Gelof filed the suit Monday in Wayne County (Mich.) Circuit Court. The complaint also names team owner Ilitch Holdings and the Detroit-Wayne County Stadium Authority, which owns the stadium.
Gelof, 26, sustained the injury while playing left field in the third inning of a 4-1 loss at Detroit on July 9.
While making a sliding catch on a foul ball, he alleges in the lawsuit that his "right knee violently struck an exposed dangerous metal fence on the side wall that protruded into or alongside the playing area."
According to a copy of the complaint obtained by the Detroit Free Press, "the collision tore plaintiff Zack Gelof's uniform and caused a deep laceration beneath his right kneecap that narrowly missed the patellar tendon."
Gelof did not return to the Athletics' lineup until a month later on Aug. 10.
The lawsuit claims the team and ballpark were negligent, noting that padding was installed in the area shortly after the incident.
"It doesn't take a stadium design expert to realize that sharp metal fencing in an area where players are required to slide and play around is a recipe for disaster like the one that occurred here," Gelof's attorney Jon Marko said in a statement. "All they had to do was put cheap padding up like they did after Zack was injured and this entire incident could have been avoided. My son's little league diamond is safer."
Gelof is seeking unspecified compensation for pain and suffering, economic loss, lost wages, emotional and mental distress, medical bills, attorney fees and other damages.
"We are aware of the lawsuit and do not comment on pending litigation," the Tigers said in a statement on Tuesday.
Gelof finished the 2026 season batting .256 with 22 home runs, 55 RBIs and 16 stolen bases in 111 games. He started 66 games at third base, 25 in the outfield, 11 at second base and two at designated hitter.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Turkey sets up council to oversee investment fund liquidations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Turkey established a fund coordination council chaired by the vice president to oversee the rapid liquidation of investment funds to protect investor rights following a recent fund crisis, the presidency said on Tuesday.
items.body:
Turkey established a fund coordination council chaired by the vice president to oversee the rapid liquidation of investment funds to protect investor rights following a recent fund crisis, the presidency said on Tuesday.
Authorities has launched an audit of recent investment fund transactions in capital markets, the presidency said.
The Capital Markets Board presented a roadmap for paying investors, based on the asset and liquidity status of funds under liquidation during a [USN:S8N3YR0AK TEXT:"meeting"] by economy officials and President Tayyip Erdogan.
The presidency said the officials discussed additional administrative and legal measures to strengthen capital markets oversight and prevent similar crises recurring.
The fund crisis erupted after suspected price manipulation in a number of thinly traded stocks triggered heavy losses and redemption pressures at investment funds.
Almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth [USN:L8N45A04Y TEXT:"$20 billion"] that authorities ordered to be liquidated this month.

items.title: Iranianos sofrem com aumento vertiginoso dos custos de sete meses de guerra
items.author: John Davison, Emily Giles
items.creator: John Davison, Emily Giles
items.summary: Os líderes do Irã podem transmitir otimismo em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos, mas a vida está se tornando cada vez mais difícil para os cidadãos comuns, que não têm condições de arcar com as necessidades básicas ou com o aluguel, à medida que o bloqueio dos EUA corta a principal fonte de renda do Estado — as exportações de petróleo.
items.body:
Os líderes do Irã podem transmitir otimismo em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos, mas a vida está se tornando cada vez mais difícil para os cidadãos comuns, que não têm condições de arcar com as necessidades básicas ou com o aluguel, à medida que o bloqueio dos EUA corta a principal fonte de renda do Estado — as exportações de petróleo.
De um engenheiro forçado a deixar Teerã devido ao alto aluguel a uma mulher obrigada a parar de fumar por causa do preço dos cigarros e cuidadores que lutam para comprar remédios, todas as áreas da vida cotidiana são afetadas.
“Sou obrigado a vender meus produtos com um lucro muito pequeno e insignificante, mas não posso fechar meu negócio porque, se o fizer, ficarei desempregado”, disse Behnam Riazi, dono de um restaurante entrevistado diante das câmeras em Teerã.
Riazi não pode aumentar seus preços porque seus clientes não podem pagar mais — e a maioria, de qualquer forma, compra apenas o essencial agora.
Não está claro até que ponto as tensões econômicas podem levar o Irã a um acordo diplomático, já que o país reforça seu próprio controle sobre as exportações de energia do Golfo pelo Estreito de Ormuz, elevando os preços do petróleo e do gás nos EUA e em todo o mundo.
MISÉRIA ECONÔMICA PODE IMPULSIONAR A DIPLOMACIA No entanto, a mais recente onda de diplomacia foi parcialmente impulsionada pelas tensões econômicas, segundo fontes dos EUA, do Oriente Médio e do Irã na semana passada. Autoridades iranianas têm expressado repetidamente temores de agitação social e reprimido impiedosamente qualquer sinal de dissidência.
Em janeiro, mais de um mês antes de os EUA e Israel iniciarem sua guerra contra o Irã, as autoridades mataram milhares de manifestantes exasperados por anos de sofrimento econômico acumulado.
Mas agora, todos com quem a Reuters conversou disseram ter preocupações diárias demais para pensar em protestar.
Hediyeh, uma dona de casa na casa dos 60 anos no norte do Irã, sobrevive com a aposentadoria do marido, que era funcionário público. Ela mal consegue pagar pelos remédios ou mesmo pelas fraldas para adultos de que sua mãe idosa, que tem Alzheimer, precisa.
Ela queria comprar uma mochila nova para o neto no primeiro dia de aula neste outono, mas o preço era cinco ou seis vezes maior do que ela esperava e, no fim, só conseguiu comprar um caderno e lápis para ele.
Como a maioria dos iranianos entrevistados pela Reuters por telefone ou por aplicativo de mensagens, ela não quis se identificar, temendo punição por falar com a mídia estrangeira.
A.J., um professor que pediu para ser identificado apenas pelas iniciais, também disse que nem sempre consegue pagar pelos remédios de que sua mãe precisa.
Ele já se mudou para morar com a mãe e os irmãos em um vilarejo no norte do país, deixando Teerã depois que as aulas passaram a ser ministradas online por causa da guerra, mas teme não ter mais condições financeiras de voltar caso as aulas presenciais sejam retomadas.
Em Sanandaj, capital da província do Curdistão, a psicoterapeuta Nazanin, de 34 anos, desistiu de fumar por causa do custo, depois de anteriormente ter achado impossível fazê-lo, disse ela.
Aqueles que têm condições de contornar as formas habituais de obter bens ou serviços por meio do mercado negro estão percebendo que ele se tornou mais difundido, embora o custo tenha aumentado.
Um homem disse ter pago US$200 em moeda forte a um cirurgião para contornar o processo burocrático necessário para uma operação.
Outro disse que os pedidos de suborno por parte da polícia estavam se tornando mais frequentes e que teve de pagar mais do que antes depois de ser parado em um posto de controle sem documentos de identificação.
CORTES DE PESSOAL NO SETOR PRIVADO Um arquiteto, que se identificou apenas pelas iniciais A.A., disse que até mesmo os iranianos mais ricos estavam cortando gastos: “Todos eles ficaram pobres em comparação com o estilo de vida que costumavam ter.”
Um pneu furou na semana passada e ele está tendo que dirigir com o pneu sobressalente durante as duas semanas que levará para conseguir um pneu de reposição barato; ele não tem mais condições de comprar aqueles disponíveis imediatamente.
Ele teme que o Irã esteja caminhando para uma escassez de combustível, o que poderia interromper as cadeias de abastecimento e causar um caos econômico ainda maior.
A guerra já está causando pesadas perdas de empregos em todo o setor privado.
M.H., uma mulher em Teerã que também pediu para ser identificada apenas pelas iniciais, disse que perdeu o emprego este mês no departamento de compras de uma empresa local, embora seu contrato de um ano tivesse sido renovado apenas no dia anterior.
Agora ela precisa devolver o dinheiro que a empresa havia depositado no sistema de previdência social do Irã para o próximo ano. Sua família estabeleceu prioridades rígidas nos gastos, com a alimentação em primeiro lugar.
“Ainda bem que ainda podemos pagar pela internet, assim podemos ficar conectados online, talvez assistir a um filme”, disse ela.
Bijan, de 40 anos, um ex-engenheiro que agora dá aulas particulares para ganhar dinheiro, disse que ele e a esposa deixaram o apartamento em Teerã e se mudaram para uma área que ele descreveu como “meia favela” nos arredores da capital.
O casal esgotou suas economias e planeja se mudar para outra cidade, onde esperam viver com menos gastos.
Os donos de lojas percebem a queda no padrão de vida melhor do que a maioria das pessoas. Ramin Yousefnia disse, em uma entrevista filmada em Teerã, que todos os clientes de seu supermercado reduziram os gastos.
“Algo que costumavam comprar em quantidades de cinco ou dez, agora só conseguem comprar dois”, disse ele. “Nem me faça falar sobre poupança. Essa é a realidade.”

items.title: Departamento de Justicia de EEUU acusa a un venezolano baleado por un agente del ICE en Austin
items.author: Julia Harte
items.creator: Julia Harte
items.summary: Un venezolano baleado por un agente federal de inmigración el 20 de septiembre en Austin, Texas, compareció el martes ante un tribunal federal tras ser acusado de agredir, resistirse, interferir y obstaculizar a un funcionario federal, informó el Departamento de Justicia.
items.body:
Un venezolano [USN:L6N45E0PF TEXT:"baleado por un agente federal de inmigración"] el 20 de septiembre en Austin, Texas, compareció el martes ante un tribunal federal tras ser acusado de agredir, resistirse, interferir y obstaculizar a un funcionario federal, informó el Departamento de Justicia.
La denuncia contra Wilber Rafael Garces Pérez, de 28 años, que cita imágenes de la cámara que llevaba uno de los agentes del ICE que lo detuvieron ese día, afirma que cuando le pidieron que saliera de su coche, arrancó y golpeó a un agente en el torso con el espejo retrovisor. El video no se ha hecho público.
Según la denuncia, presentada el lunes ante el Tribunal de Distrito para el Distrito Oeste de Texas, el agente, que no llevaba cámara, persiguió a Garces Pérez en su coche y pronto lo alcanzó.
En ese momento, Garces Pérez intentó atropellar al agente, quien le disparó con su pistola, según la denuncia.
Los videos del incidente disponibles públicamente no muestran el tiroteo, pero sí muestran a Garces Pérez herido en el auto después.
Según la denuncia, Garces Pérez le dijo al funcionario del DHS que investigaba el caso que le dispararon después de que un agente estrellara su camioneta contra su auto, haciéndolo girar.
El abogado de Garces Pérez no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios. Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch publicó en Instagram el domingo que su cliente aún tiene la bala alojada en el cuerpo y una clavícula fracturada, y que [USN:L6N45G13E TEXT:"sus allegados"] están preocupados de que pueda sufrir sepsis y daños permanentes si no se somete a cirugía pronto.
El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional ha declarado que está recibiendo la atención médica adecuada.
Si bien el Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha presentado cargos penales contra al menos 851 personas por atacar o entorpecer la labor de agentes federales, una [USN:L6N43V0Z5 TEXT:"revisión de los registros de los tribunales realizada por Reuters"] en julio reveló que el 31% de los casos concluidos habían sido desestimados, frente a una tasa de desestimación del 8% de todos los casos penales federales.
Garces Pérez tiene previsto comparecer el miércoles ante un juez federal de inmigración en Texas para una audiencia en la que se determinará si puede permanecer en el país.

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Comissão Reguladora Nuclear dos EUA (NRC) aprovou uma licença de construção para a Tennessee Valley Authority construir o primeiro reator modular pequeno comercial do país, informou a agência nesta terça-feira.
items.body:
A Comissão Reguladora Nuclear dos EUA (NRC) aprovou uma licença de construção para a Tennessee Valley Authority (TVC.N) construir o primeiro reator modular pequeno comercial do país, informou a agência nesta terça-feira.
“A TVA planeja construir um reator de água fervente da GE Vernova Hitachi de 300 megawatts para ajudar a atender à crescente demanda regional por energia”, afirmou a agência em comunicado.
Os reatores de água fervente utilizam o calor da fissão nuclear para ferver a água dentro do vaso do reator, produzindo vapor que aciona diretamente uma turbina para gerar eletricidade.
O projeto recebeu licença de construção após a NRC concluir uma análise de 14 meses, marcando a segunda grande aprovação de reator pela agência neste ano, informou a agência.
A TVA precisará de uma licença de operação separada da NRC antes de carregar o combustível e iniciar as operações, informou a agência. A TVA já havia recebido uma licença preliminar para o local da usina em 2019.
(Por Noel John)

items.title: Anthropic’s $2 trln goal is AI’s biggest moonshot
items.author: Karen Kwok
items.creator: Karen Kwok
items.summary: The Claude maker posted big growth and a 40% gross margin last year, but also an $8 bln operating loss. Its 2026 figures will groan further under huge spending promises to feed demand. Even next to recently launched frenemy SpaceX, CEO Dario Amodei’s valuation target looks steep.
items.body:
Anthropic hopes to ramp up a season for gargantuan public debuts started by SpaceX (SPCX.O) . In doing so, the artificial intelligence lab behind Claude will push investors to accept yet wilder financial ambitions. Key details from the company’s IPO prospectus offer a glimpse at tantalizingly massive growth to support a $2 trillion valuation target, as [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"reported"] by Reuters. They also make even Elon Musk’s rockets-to-robots concern look down to Earth.
According to documents reviewed by Reuters, Anthropic's revenue rose nearly 12-fold in 2025, to $4.6 billion. Its implied gross margin, or revenue less costs mostly comprised of computing responses to user queries, swung to roughly 40% last year, from negative 95%, an extraordinary turnaround.
The hope is that continued rapid growth can further pay off boss Dario Amodei’s massive investments in computing power. While full details of this year’s results are yet to emerge, take the company’s $16 billion in [USN:L6N41Y0ZA TEXT:"revenue"] in the first and second quarters, and assume it holds steady. That should lead to just shy of $40 billion in sales for all of 2026, before accounting for any further spurts.
At a $2 trillion valuation, less $120 billion of net cash as reported by The Information, Anthropic would be worth roughly 47 times that revenue. That would exceed SpaceX's already sky-high multiple of about 42 times expected sales this year, based on Visible Alpha data.
Moreover, 83% of Anthropic’s 2025 revenue was from metered consumption, up from 75% in 2024. Such customers can cut usage quickly if budgets tighten or cheaper, alternative models emerge. And although last year’s figures miss much of the boost from the “vibe coding” phenomenon sparked by Claude Code, recent innovations by rival Meta Platforms (META.O) in offering AI agents for ordinary tasks may push growth into the consumer end of the market, where Anthropic has a weaker hand.
Then there’s the continued, massive spending on data centers to train models. Anthropic spent over $7 billion on computing infrastructure in 2025, or $1.60 for every dollar of revenue. Granted, it spent $6.53 per dollar of revenue in 2024, but last year still saw an $8 billion operating loss.
Anthropic also points to over $500 billion in spending commitments spread across multi-year contracts. Big chunks of that sum, agreed to with Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Google, Amazon.com (AMZN.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) , cannot just be walked away from. A more flexible arrangement with SpaceX came at [USN:L6N42414K TEXT:"heavy cost"]. To boot, these are both partners and rivals, who might reprioritize in-house AI efforts.
Amodei can point to faster growth than even Musk’s company, but has no ballast like a quasi-monopolistic rocket empire. If Anthropic’s growth continues to largely enrich its frenemies, the company’s own valuation ambitions will begin to look starry-eyed.
Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X .
Artificial intelligence lab Anthropic's revenue grew 12-fold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, according to details of an IPO prospectus reported by Reuters.
Anthropic reported a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, and plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years, according to the documents.

items.title: 英中銀の利上げ根拠「乏しい」、エネ高のインフレ波及見極めへ＝テイラー委員
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ロンドン　２９日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[ロンドン　２９日　ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のテイラー金融政策委員は２９日、エネルギー価格の高騰が幅広い経済分野へのインフレ波及として明確に表れない限り、利上げの根拠は乏しいままだとの見解を示した。

テイラー氏は英国立経済社会研究所の講演で、「エネルギー価格が長期間にわたって高止まりし、より広範なインフレの持続性への波及を示すより明確なシグナルが生じない限り、さらなる利上げの根拠は私にとって説得力を持たない」と述べた。

現在の見通しについて、ロシアのウクライナ全面侵攻によって原油価格が急騰し、コロナ禍後の労働市場の逼迫に拍車をかけ、インフレを２桁台に押し上げた２０２２年の状況とは類似していないと指摘。

「これほど目に見えるエネルギーショックの後、多くのエネルギー集約型の財（モノ）・サービス分野におけるインフレは、予想されたほど加速していない」と述べた。 

テイラー氏はまた、追加利上げがあるとの根拠のない市場観測をあおることなく、英中銀がインフレ抑制のために１回だけ利上げを行うことが現実的かどうかは不明だとの見方も示した。

テイラー氏はさらに、２０２７年の企業の賃金見通しに関する英中銀の年次調査が、利上げの是非を判断する上で鍵になるとの認識を示した。「来年１月に公表予定の２７年の賃金見通しに関する調査は、非常に重要なデータポイントとなる」と述べた。

また、英中銀の１２月会合の時点で入手可能な暫定結果にも注目すると説明。前回調査の水準である３％をやや上回る程度、あるいはそれ以下の数値であれば、インフレ圧力が抑制されているとの安心材料になると述べた。

items.title: At UN, developing nations call for bigger say in shaping AI future
items.author: Doyinsola Oladipo
items.creator: Doyinsola Oladipo
items.summary: Developing nations are demanding a greater role in shaping the rules governing artificial intelligence, warning that a technology poised to transform economies could instead deepen global inequalities if its development and regulation remain concentrated in wealthy countries.
items.body:
Developing nations are demanding a greater role in shaping the rules governing artificial intelligence, warning that a technology poised to transform economies could instead deepen global inequalities if its development and regulation remain concentrated in wealthy countries.
The debate at last week's UN festival of diplomacy in New York highlighted [USN:FWN4560E8 TEXT:"mounting concern"] among leaders from Africa, Asia and Latin America around the increasingly powerful technology after several safety breaches, and as top researchers have warned it could destroy humanity.
"Developing countries cannot be reduced to the role of mere users of technologies designed elsewhere, nor should be the mere recipients of standards and norms that they did not adequately participate in shaping," said Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
"We must ensure that technological transformations of the 21st century do not reproduce the economic imbalances of previous decades," Wagner said.
She made the remarks at a Security Council session [USN:L6N45E0VV TEXT:"dedicated to AI"] that featured top executives of leading labs, including Sam Altman from OpenAI and Dario Amodei from Anthropic, who urged governments to work together to manage the technology.
Underscoring the surge in interest in the subject, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh, who chaired the UN debate this year, said that, "four years ago, AI was raised in this hall by only five delegations – this year, 128 delegations addressed it."
'A QUESTION OF GOVERNANCE' "Many framed AI as a question of governance: Who designs it, who benefits? Who bears the risks, and who is accountable when harm occurs," added the Bangladeshi foreign minister as he concluded the marathon of speeches at the UN.
AI could enable developing countries to gain a century's worth of development in a decade if they act quickly on power, connectivity and skills gaps, the World Bank [USN:L8N4401YH TEXT:"said in a report last month"].
The International Monetary Fund said in July that AI [USN:L6N43M0EG TEXT:"could boost"] Sub-Saharan Africa's economy by about 4% over the next decade under the right circumstances.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres compared debates around AI risks and climate change and said that developing nations should have an equal voice in both.
"The climate crisis went from distant warning to daily reality and artificial intelligence moved at a speed that has blindsided even those who created it," he said.
"These are not separate crises. They are chapters of the same story, the story of power: Who has it. Who is denied it. How it is used. And how it is changing," Guterres told the UN.
As with climate change, Guterres and Global South leaders urged a coordinated global action rather than isolated national responses to AI threats.
Their focus on regulation stood in sharp contrast with remarks by US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed AI risks as a "hoax" and "sick conspiracy" and told the UN that – like climate change – they were vastly overblown.
“The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming – a name since reborn to climate change because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead – these are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all," Trump said.
Belize Prime Minister John Briceño said AI, if well governed, could widen access to knowledge and improve public services. But he also warned: "Poorly governed, it can deepen inequality, expose critical systems, displace workers and leave developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere.”

items.title: Diesel prices poised to hit consumers even harder
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Diesel prices are on a big upward swing, rising to historic levels over the past month and filtering through to all corners of the economy.
items.body: Diesel prices rose to historic levels over the past month, filtering through to all corners of the economy as shippers and consumers struggle to absorb the blow. Retail diesel topped $2.64 per litre on average for the week ended Tuesday, up 59 per cent from right before the Iran war and 15 per cent from November 2022, which held the price record until this year. Supply disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have shrunk energy output for seven months and counting, with the critical waterway effectively closed and many crude refineries slashing production. Experts say elevated fuel costs mean higher price tags on items ranging from food and clothing to construction materials for months to come, with diesel demand poised to go up further as winter approaches. The price of a round-trip haul by a semi truck between Montreal and Toronto would have cost roughly $850 on Jan. 1. Now the total would amount to $1,400, said Mike Millian, president of the Private Motor Truck Council of Canada. “A fleet’s No. 1 expense outside of wages was always fuel. Now it’s probably fuel,” said Millian, whose group represents about 200 companies with in-house fleets including Tim Hortons, Home Hardware and Loblaw. “It’s really dramatic. It’s tough to to absorb.” Diesel powers industries ranging from agriculture to mining and manufacturing, and the bigger expenses they face are likely to show up as higher sticker prices on consumer items. “It hurts everybody. There’s not anybody this doesn’t affect,” said Millian. Even if a deal to open the strait were struck tomorrow, consumers would likely wait months before prices fell. That lag stems partly from the time needed to carry out major shifts in a creaky global supply chain, from reopening oil wells to shipping crude oil to refineries. “It’s almost like a very slow-moving train where, when you stop it, getting going again has its own challenges,” said Ross Prentice, co-founder of Evotrux, an online platform connecting shippers and carriers. Freight railway fuel surcharges for October now sit up to 73 per cent above levels from early August, according to figures from Canadian National Railway Co. and Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd. Truckers who haul produce, clothes and pharmaceuticals across the continent to Canadian shelves tack on surcharges as well. But there is often a gap between the transport time and the date the weekly fuel charges are pegged to. “Fuel may have jumped 10 cents since yesterday, and they’re hauling it for the same amount,” said Millian. “A couple of cents a week used to be a big deal. Now it might move 10 cents from the time you get up to the time you go to bed.” The shippers and retailers who face those transport surcharges often find they have little choice but to raise prices for shoppers. “If you’re an independent grocer and you’re on an overall margin of two per cent and you’re getting fuel surcharges from your suppliers, you’re in a tough spot,” said Gary Sands, a senior vice-president at the Canadian Federation of Independent Grocers, which represents about 6,900 stores. “It becomes very difficult to not pass on those fuel surcharges.” --- Christopher Reynolds, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 29, 2026.

items.title: Ken Paxton's 2022 remarks on Uvalde school shooting clipped to omit context
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Audio from a 2022 interview with US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a Texas Republican, is edited to omit the context of his full remarks about the Uvalde school shooting and misleadingly shared online as “newly uncovered.”
items.body:
Audio from a 2022 interview with US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a Texas Republican, is edited to omit the context of his full remarks about the Uvalde school shooting and misleadingly shared online as “newly uncovered.”
Paxton, who is running in a [USN:L6N44T0XY TEXT:"tight race"] against Democrat James Talarico, was the Texas attorney general on May 24, 2022, when an 18-year-old gunman [USN:S0N2XF01A TEXT:"killed 19 students"] and two teachers at Texas’ Robb Elementary School before being [USN:L1N3YN02M TEXT:"shot dead"] by law enforcement.
Paxton addressed the shooting in the second segment of the May 29, 2022, Smart Talk with Trey Graham podcast .
An excerpt from that podcast appears in a September 23 X post captioned, “NEWLY UNCOVERED AUDIO: Texas GOP US Senate candidate Ken Paxton calls the Uvalde shooting a ‘plan’ by ‘God’ and says ‘life is short’ about children murdered in an elementary school. This man is vile.”
The audio clip in the post includes Paxton saying, “Look, there's always a plan. I believe God always has a plan. Life is short no matter what it is.”
However, in the podcast, Graham, a North Texas pastor, asked Paxton to share any words of comfort or encouragement to the families who lost their children in the shooting.
Paxton, who opposes gun control , said, “It's difficult to give comfort. If I, if I lost one of my children, I'd be pretty devastated, especially in a, in a way that is so senseless and, you know, seemingly has no purpose. I, I think I would, I would just have to, if, if, if I had the opportunity to talk to people, I'd have to say, ‘Look, there's always a plan. I believe God always has a plan. Life is short no matter what it is, and certainly, we, we're not gonna make sense of, you know, a young child being shot, and killed way before their life expectancy. And so even though we can't make sense of it, I would just have to encourage them to hold onto their faith and to hold onto their belief that there really is purpose in, in what God does. And we may not know it now, but someday we will.”
The owner of the X account that posted the excerpt told Reuters by email that Paxton’s remarks were “widely reported on at the time” as insensitive and shared links to articles describing the backlash. She did not respond to questions about the source of the short clip, which her post describes as “newly uncovered audio.”
A spokesperson for Graham declined to comment but also referred Reuters to a 2022 opinion piece in the Washington Post titled, “Texas AG Paxton’s shameful Uvalde cop-out: ‘God always has a plan'.”
Paxton’s office and campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
VERDICT Missing context. An audio excerpt of 2022 remarks by Ken Paxton about the Uvalde school shooting is not “newly uncovered” and omits the full context of his response to a podcaster’s question.
This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

items.title: ANP avança para reduzir concentração no mercado de gás apesar de resistência da Petrobras
items.author: Rodrigo Viga Gaier, Marta Nogueira
items.creator: Rodrigo Viga Gaier, Marta Nogueira
items.summary: A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) deu mais um passo em direção à implementação do programa de "gas release", iniciativa do governo que visa reduzir a concentração do mercado brasileiro de gás natural e a predominância da Petrobras no setor, indicaram discussões sobre o tema nesta terça-feira.
items.body:
A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) deu mais um passo em direção à implementação do programa de "gas release", iniciativa do governo que visa reduzir a concentração do mercado brasileiro de gás natural e a predominância da Petrobras no setor, indicaram discussões sobre o tema nesta terça-feira.
Na véspera, a ANP encerrou uma consulta pública sobre a proposta, apesar de resistência da estatal, que voltou a pedir um adiamento das discussões nesta terça-feira.
O programa do "gas release" prevê a realização de leilões regulados pela autarquia para oferta de volumes de gás hoje adquiridos pela Petrobras de terceiros produtores ou importados da Bolívia, permitindo que outros comercializadores tenham acesso a esses volumes e concorram com a estatal na venda do combustível.
Durante workshop promovido pela reguladora nesta terça-feira, representantes do governo, da ANP e da indústria reforçaram o apoio à iniciativa, prevista na Lei do Gás, argumentando que a abertura do mercado ocorrida nos últimos anos ainda não foi suficiente para eliminar a elevada concentração na oferta do combustível.
Segundo estudo apresentado pela ANP, a Petrobras ainda detém participação média de 59% no mercado atacadista não termelétrico atendido pela malha integrada de transporte.
Também presente no evento, o gerente-executivo de gás e energia da Petrobras, Álvaro Tupiassú, reiterou que a companhia não vê necessidade de implementar o "gas release" neste momento, argumentando que a participação da estatal no mercado já vem caindo nos últimos anos.
Tupiassú defendeu ainda um pedido de adiamento da audiência pública sobre o tema, prevista atualmente para 21 de outubro. A audiência é o último passo antes que a agência decida sobre o formato definitivo do programa.
"Achamos que essa discussão tem que levar mais tempo e que é possível levar mais tempo sem comprometer o eventual objetivo de fazer vigência (do programa) em 2028", afirmou Tupiassú, durante participação no workshop.
Durante o congresso ROG.e, na semana passada, a presidente da Petrobras, Magda Chambriard, defendeu a atuação da companhia como compradora de gás de terceiros, afirmando que esse tipo de arranjo ajuda a viabilizar investimentos e é comum em outros mercados.
O diretor da autarquia, Pietro Mendes, entretanto, rebateu os pedidos de adiamento da Petrobras e afirmou que "cabe à ANP pensar no todo... não para maximizar o interesse do monopolista, mas sim para maximizar o interesse da sociedade brasileira".
O diretor acrescentou que a agência "não pode se conformar com o preço do gás natural que temos no Brasil".
"A gente já analisou o pedido de adiamento e já houve um julgamento pela diretoria colegiada, por unanimidade, de não adiar a audiência pública", afirmou, ponderando que até poderia avaliar novo pedido, mas que os fundamentos não são oportunos.
Pietro também criticou os argumentos usados para defender uma postergação das discussões.
"A gente não pode aceitar prorrogação por argumentos maniqueístas, do bem e do mal. 'A agência má que está colocando em discussão o gas release, a agência está adotando uma medida que é absurda por si só', sem que a gente tenha um espaço para debate", disse.
Segundo ele, a ANP precisa ter sua competência técnica respeitada e não pode ser impedida de discutir medidas previstas na legislação para aumentar a concorrência no mercado de gás.
O secretário de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis do Ministério de Minas e Energia, Renato Dutra, afirmou que o programa está alinhado à política energética do governo e faz parte de uma agenda mais ampla voltada ao aumento da oferta e à redução dos preços do gás para a indústria brasileira.
A iniciativa integra o programa Gás para Empregar, lançado pelo governo Lula com o objetivo de ampliar a oferta de gás natural e reduzir custos para consumidores industriais.
items.raw_description: A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) deu mais um passo em direção à implementação do programa de "gas release", iniciativa do governo que visa reduzir a concentração do mercado brasileiro de gás natural e a predominância da Petrobras no setor, indicaram discussões sobre o tema nesta terça-feira.

items.title: Five things to know about the college sports bill that passed the US Senate
items.author: Nolan Mccaskill
items.creator: Nolan Mccaskill
items.summary: The US Senate passed legislation this week to regulate college sports, a multibillion-dollar industry that has been upended in recent years by increased earning opportunities for student athletes.
items.body:
The US Senate passed legislation this week to regulate college sports, a multibillion-dollar industry that has been upended in recent years by increased earning opportunities for student athletes.
Here are five things to know about the bill's passage:
WHAT JUST HAPPENED? The Senate voted 77-22 on Monday evening to pass the proposal, which now heads to the US House of Representatives.
HOW WOULD IT CHANGE COLLEGE SPORTS? The proposal would create national standards around student athlete transfers, eligibility and compensation for name, image and likeness use.
It would permit one school transfer "without losing or delaying eligibility to participate." A student athlete who transferred institutions a second time would be ineligible for one year aside from four exceptions including the departure of a head coach, sexual assault or harassment and the discontinuation of a sport.
Student athletes would also be limited to five years of eligibility with exceptions for pregnancy, religious missions, active-duty military service and a "serious athletic injury or medical condition."
The measure would protect student athletes' rights to NIL compensation and require disclosure of NIL deals that exceed $600.
IS IT CONTROVERSIAL? The legislation includes several controversial components. For example, its national standards on transfers, eligibility and name, image and likeness deals would preempt state laws. More than 30 states have already enacted their own name, image and likeness laws.
The bill sidesteps one of college sports' biggest legal battles: whether the athletes should be classified as employees rather than students participating in extracurricular activities.
The proposal allows athletes to sue to enforce its provisions, rather than requiring arbitration, though critics say lawsuits are burdensome to individuals.
"Student-athletes often have limited time, resources, and legal expertise," Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, a Delaware Democrat, said in a statement. "They should not bear primary responsibility for identifying violations and suing their schools or athletic programs to secure the protections provided by the bill."
Blunt Rochester also warned that Congress should not lock in terms "that could limit student-athletes' ability to negotiate or collectively bargain over them in the future."
WHO VOTED FOR IT? Fifty of the chamber's 53 Republicans supported the legislation. Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska did not vote. Senators Rick Scott of Florida and Rand Paul of Kentucky opposed it. Paul proposed an amendment that would have gutted the bill. Paul's amendment was overwhelmingly rejected, failing 1-94 with only Paul voting in favor of it.
Twenty-seven members of the Democratic Caucus backed the legislation.
Opponents said the measure could limit athletes' leverage in future labor and antitrust disputes, even as it created new health, safety and compensation protections.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? The measure now moves to the House, which has recessed until after November 3's midterm elections. A majority of the 433-member House — two seats are vacant — would have to approve the bill to send it to President Donald Trump's desk to be signed into law.

items.title: Trump government ads draw artist protest, regulatory complaints
items.author: Dawn Kopecki, Helen Coster
items.creator: Dawn Kopecki, Helen Coster
items.summary: Taxpayer-funded television ads featuring President Donald Trump drew fresh scrutiny on Tuesday after the recording artist behind a song used in one spot demanded the White House stop using his music and a watchdog group asked federal regulators to pull the commercials from the air.
items.body:
Taxpayer-funded television ads featuring President Donald Trump drew fresh scrutiny on Tuesday after the recording artist behind a song used in one spot demanded the White House stop using his music and a watchdog group asked federal regulators to pull the commercials from the air.
The developments added to growing criticism of the three nationally broadcast ads, which celebrate a "golden age of America" and are airing five weeks before midterm elections, with ethics experts and lawmakers from both parties questioning whether public funds are being used to promote Trump politically.
Attorneys for Christian Berishaj, who performs as JMSN, sent the White House a cease-and-desist letter saying his song "Love Me" was used without permission, while Public Citizen filed complaints with regulators arguing the spots are campaign advertisements that should not be produced or distributed with taxpayer resources.
Democratic Senators Patty Murray and Chris Murphy asked Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Tuesday to answer for the ads, saying the administration had diverted $20 million from the agency for the ad campaign.
"This administration’s defense of using Americans’ tax dollars to air these ads is as absurd as it is offensive," they wrote in a letter to Mullin.
The White House did not immediately respond to Reuters questions on Tuesday about the cost of the ads or criticism that they amount to political advertising funded by taxpayers. It previously defended the spots as "public service announcements" intended to promote patriotism rather than campaign ads.
The ads end with the disclaimer "Paid for by the US Government."
'LOVE ME,' THE ADS IMPLORE One ad features Trump declaring that "America will never be a communist country" while a chorus repeats the words "love me." Another combines images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a "golden age of America." A third describes a "final battle" against the "deep state" and closely resembles one of Trump's 2024 campaign advertisements.
Berishaj said in an Instagram post that he would "never authorize my music to be used for ANY political agenda or campaign."
Public Citizen asked broadcasters to stop airing the spots and urged federal authorities to investigate whether executive branch officials improperly engaged in partisan political activity.
"These ads are campaign advertisements, which should be produced and distributed on campaign time and without involving taxpayer dollars," the group said.
Critics say the spots may violate longstanding restrictions on government propaganda and political activity.

items.title: OpenAI desafia Meta com agente Dots, que funciona ininterruptamente, em sua iniciativa de IA empresarial
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A OpenAI apresentou nesta terça-feira agentes sempre ativos chamados Dots, que perseguem objetivos do usuário em diversos aplicativos de forma autônoma, intensificando sua investida no lucrativo mercado corporativo e competindo diretamente com a Meta na corrida para vender IA que possa funcionar de forma autônoma.
items.body:
A OpenAI apresentou nesta terça-feira agentes sempre ativos chamados Dots, que perseguem objetivos do usuário em diversos aplicativos de forma autônoma, intensificando sua investida no lucrativo mercado corporativo e competindo diretamente com a Meta (META.O) na corrida para vender IA que possa funcionar de forma autônoma.
Os agentes da Dots visam capitalizar a crescente demanda por agentes capazes de lidar com tarefas cotidianas com pouca supervisão. O interesse por essas ferramentas aumentou consideravelmente desde que o Muse, da Meta, atraiu milhões de downloads no início deste mês e impulsionou as ações de empresas que, segundo investidores, podem se beneficiar ou ser impactadas por serviços autônomos de IA.
A OpenAI lançou o agente em seu evento anual para desenvolvedores em San Francisco nesta terça-feira, aproveitando também para destacar sua crescente presença no mercado corporativo e junto aos consumidores, um sinal de que a boa aceitação do modelo Astra permitiu que a empresa recuperasse terreno na corrida da IA.
A notícia surge um dia depois de a OpenAI ter suspendido o lançamento de um modelo Astra mais poderoso, alegando que este demonstrava uma alta disposição para enganar os usuários sobre suas ações. A empresa está sob escrutínio depois de seus agentes de IA terem invadido os serviços da Hugging Face e de um website de saúde do governo australiano durante testes internos.
Crescer rapidamente é crucial para os planos da OpenAI de investir dezenas de bilhões de dólares em data centers de IA e acompanhar rivais como a Anthropic e a Meta. A empresa, que impulsionou o boom da IA com o ChatGPT no final de 2022, também está se preparando para um IPO que pode avaliá-la em mais de US$1 trilhão. A rival Anthropic pode valer US$2 trilhões quando abrir seu capital.
GERENCIANDO PROJETOS EM EVOLUÇÃO Os Dots utilizam o modelo avançado GPT-6 Astra da OpenAI e conseguem gerenciar projetos à medida que evoluem, como atualizar uma proposta de vendas quando as necessidades do cliente mudam e criar uma demonstração funcional para revisão. Os usuários podem se comunicar com os Dots no Slack e no Teams, e os agentes podem utilizar as ferramentas Codex e ChatGPT Work da OpenAI para pesquisar, analisar dados, preparar documentos e desenvolver software.
Na terça-feira, a OpenAI destacou as medidas de segurança incorporadas ao Dots. Afirmou que os usuários podem definir regras personalizadas que determinam o que o Dots pode fazer e quando os agentes devem solicitar permissão, acrescentando que tarefas sensíveis, como alterar senhas e excluir dados permanentemente, exigem o consentimento explícito do usuário.
A empresa também afirmou que os Dots funcionam em seus próprios computadores em nuvem e que estava implementando ferramentas de inteligência privada para verificar riscos de segurança sem reter os dados de clientes corporativos.
Vários executivos de tecnologia, incluindo Alex Karp, presidente-executivo da Palantir (PLTR.O) , afirmaram nos últimos meses que as companhias precisam ter certeza de que as empresas de IA não estão retendo seus dados, especialmente em setores regulamentados como saúde e finanças.
A Reuters informou na sexta-feira que a OpenAI ainda estava trabalhando para entender a extensão total da atividade de seus agentes desonestos, dois meses após o ataque à Hugging Face, sendo o exemplo mais recente o vazamento de 53 imagens de usuários do ChatGPT, segundo a própria startup.
A OpenAI reiterou na terça-feira que não utiliza, por padrão, os dados de seus clientes corporativos para treinar sua IA e que os usuários do plano pessoal podem optar por não compartilhar conversas e trabalhos do Dots usados para treinamento.
O número de usuários semanais do Codex e do ChatGPT Work ultrapassou 35 milhões, um aumento significativo em relação aos cerca de 5 milhões de usuários do Codex em junho, informou a empresa nesta terça-feira. Já o ChatGPT, voltado para o consumidor, agora conta com mais de 1,2 bilhão de usuários semanais.
A empresa está lançando uma série de novas ofertas, incluindo um espaço de trabalho compartilhado para equipes de negócios e IA chamado ChatGPT Space, o modelo GPT-6.1 Sol mais acessível e um plano Pro de US$500 que oferece maior uso e desempenho mais rápido.
(Por Deepa Seetharaman e Aditya Soni)

items.title: BP proposes six-year labor contract at Whiting refinery
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: BP said on Tuesday it is proposing a six-year labor contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana as negotiations with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 continue.
items.body:
BP (BP.L) said on Tuesday it is proposing a six-year labor contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana as negotiations with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 continue.
The company said the six-year term would provide stability for the refinery and employees.
"6-year term would give you certainty in your pay, your benefits, and your working conditions for years," BP said.
The final two years of the proposed agreement would match future National Oil Bargaining Program (NOBP) pattern wage-rate increases.
BP is also proposing a longer notice period before the union can strike or the company can initiate a lockout.
The company said it would continue talks with USW 7-1 representatives.
BP [USN:L6N42Y162 TEXT:"locked out"] its workers at the Whiting refinery in March in a dispute with the union over its next contract.

items.title: OpenAI targets $30 billion funding at $1.4 trillion valuation, Bloomberg News reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round and is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, not including the money raised, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
items.body:
OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round and is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, not including the money raised, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Here are more details:
The fundraising discussions are at an early stage and terms could change, Bloomberg reported, adding that the demand for the round is being led by investors.
The proposed round would serve as a bridge financing to provide capital in place of an IPO, the report said.
OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The company had closed a funding round in March with $122 billion in committed capital, valuing it at $852 billion.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said [USN:L6N45500D TEXT:"earlier this month"] that the company would not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.
OpenAI's [USN:L4N45L1EC TEXT:"annualized revenue run rate"] is nearing $70 billion, having risen more than 70% since the beginning of the third quarter, Reuters reported earlier on Tuesday.

Sept 29 : OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round and is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, not including the money raised, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Here are more details:
• The fundraising discussions are at an early stage and terms could change, Bloomberg reported, adding that the demand for the round is being led by investors.
• The proposed round would serve as a bridge financing to provide capital in place of an IPO, the report said.

• OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
• The company had closed a funding round in March with $122 billion in committed capital, valuing it at $852 billion.
• OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said earlier this month that the company would not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.
• OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate is nearing $70 billion, having risen more than 70 per cent since the beginning of the third quarter, Reuters reported earlier on Tuesday.

items.title: EUA impõem sanções a 10 pessoas e entidades por suposta aquisição de armas para o Irã
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Os Estados Unidos impuseram sanções a 10 pessoas físicas e jurídicas, incluindo algumas sediadas na China, em Hong Kong e no Paquistão, por ajudarem o Ministério da Defesa do Irã a adquirir armas e componentes, informou o Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA nesta terça-feira.
items.body:
Os Estados Unidos impuseram sanções a 10 pessoas físicas e jurídicas, incluindo algumas sediadas na China, em Hong Kong e no Paquistão, por ajudarem o Ministério da Defesa do Irã a adquirir armas e componentes, informou o Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA nesta terça-feira.
As sanções fazem parte de uma iniciativa mais ampla do governo Trump para isolar economicamente o Irã e forçá-lo a negociar o fim da guerra entre os EUA e o Irã, que começou em fevereiro.
“No âmbito da Operação Economic Outcast, o Tesouro continuará a identificar e neutralizar aqueles que fornecem apoio material, tecnológico ou financeiro que permita ao regime iraniano sustentar suas atividades terroristas”, afirmou o secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent. “O Tesouro não tolerará qualquer apoio ao regime e continuará a identificar, expor e isolar aqueles que facilitam as ações do Irã.”
O Tesouro afirmou que as sanções visam enfraquecer a capacidade de Teerã de reconstituir seus programas de armamento, ao mesmo tempo em que aumentam os custos para aqueles que apoiam seus esforços de aquisição.

items.title: Goolsbee de la Fed: inflación alta durante tanto tiempo es "jugar con fuego"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el martes que permitir que la inflación se mantenga por encima del objetivo durante cinco años y medio es "jugar con fuego", y señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a responder a una perturbación de la oferta con efectos duraderos.
items.body:
El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el martes que permitir que la inflación se mantenga por encima del objetivo durante cinco años y medio es "jugar con fuego", y señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a responder a una perturbación de la oferta con efectos duraderos.
"Es una situación desagradable (...) pero creo que tenemos que plantearnos responder a esas perturbaciones persistentes", afirmó el funcionario.
Goolsbee señaló que es uno de los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed más optimistas en lo que respecta a sus expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés, pero antes de recortarlas "tenemos que obtener pruebas de que la inflación está volviendo a bajar, de que estos factores que se supone que son temporales están, de hecho, desapareciendo".

items.title: US drug lobby group PhRMA names former House leader Cantor as CEO
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The US pharmaceutical lobby group Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America said on Tuesday it had named former US House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as its next president and chief executive officer.
items.body:
The US pharmaceutical lobby group Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America said on Tuesday it had named former US House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as its next president and chief executive officer.
Cantor, who served in the US House of Representatives from 2000 to 2014, will take over on November 9, PhRMA said.
He succeeds [USN:L4N40R1K5 TEXT:"Stephen J. Ubl"], who has led the organization since 2015, a period in which the pharmaceutical industry faced pressure from US administrations and lawmakers over prescription drug pricing, market access and regulation.
PhRMA credited Cantor with backing the Medicare Part D prescription drug program, rare pediatric disease research funding and the 21st Century Cures Act during his time in Congress.
Rob Davis, PhRMA board chair and CEO of Merck (MRK.N) , said in a statement that Cantor had experience in business, policy and politics.
Ubl will remain as a strategic adviser until mid-January 2027 to assist with the transition.

items.title: US appeals court mulls contempt probe over Trump deportation flights
items.author: Jan Wolfe
items.creator: Jan Wolfe
items.summary: A US Justice Department lawyer asked an appeals court on Tuesday to terminate a judge's inquiry into whether Trump administration officials willfully violated a judicial order directing them to stop deportation flights of Venezuelan immigrants to El Salvador.
items.body:
A US Justice Department lawyer asked an appeals court on Tuesday to terminate a judge's inquiry into whether Trump administration officials willfully violated a judicial order directing them to stop deportation flights of Venezuelan immigrants to El Salvador.
The three-hour oral argument was the latest development in a long-running standoff between President Donald Trump and US District Judge James Boasberg, who has sought to determine why his order was ignored, in a dispute that has become a test of the judiciary's power to investigate executive branch decision-making.
DOJ attorney Brett Shumate told the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit during an oral argument in Washington that the criminal contempt probe by Boasberg was "unlawful, unnecessary, and futile."
"The district court judge here is going beyond the judicial role," Shumate added.
A three-judge D.C. Circuit panel [USN:L1N40X0ST TEXT:"blocked"] Boasberg's contempt probe in a 2-1 ruling earlier this year, but all 11 of the sitting judges on the intermediate court voted to rehear the case. The prominent appeals court has seven Democratic appointees and four Republican appointees.
Some of the judges on Tuesday appeared skeptical of Shumate's arguments, saying Boasberg had properly invoked a federal rule of criminal procedure that allows a judge to investigate defiance of a court order and refer the matter for prosecution.
Circuit Judge J. Michelle Childs, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden , said Boasberg was simply conducting "fact-finding to know what happened and know why there was a violation of the district court's order, oral and written."
"The district court has to find out what happened and who was in the room providing the advice," said Circuit Judge Patricia Millett, who was appointed by Democratic President Barack Obama.
The dispute arose as part of a lawsuit brought by the American Civil Liberties Union on behalf of Venezuelan men deported by the Trump administration under the Alien Enemies Act, with the plaintiffs arguing that the administration acted unlawfully with the deportation flights.
The 1798 law, which has been invoked rarely in US history, gives presidents broad powers to detain and deport non-citizens.
The Venezuelan men at the center of the litigation were [USN:L6N3TF0MG TEXT:"released"] from a Salvadoran prison last year and returned to Venezuela as part of a US-brokered prisoner swap.
Boasberg concluded last year that the administration appeared to have acted "in bad faith" when it hurriedly assembled three deportation flights at the same time that he was conducting emergency court proceedings to assess the legality of the effort.
The judge sought testimony from a high-ranking Justice Department lawyer, as well as a former department attorney who became a whistleblower.
In the 2-1 ruling issued in April, the three-judge panel said Boasberg's request had encroached on "the autonomy of the executive branch" and "proposes to probe high-level Executive Branch deliberations about matters of national security and diplomacy."
ACLU lawyer Lee Gelernt said during the hearing that Boasberg had acted courageously and refused to allow the executive branch to thumb its nose at him.
"No prior DOJ or administrator has ever taken these kinds of egregious actions and been so disrespectful to the judiciary," Gelernt said.
"If you don't uphold what this district court did, it will send a horrible message," he said.

items.title: UK's Burnham restores some hope, but near-term fixes prove elusive
items.author: Elizabeth Piper, Andrew Macaskill, Alistair Smout
items.creator: Elizabeth Piper, Andrew Macaskill, Alistair Smout
items.summary: Andy Burnham has restored some hope to his governing Labour Party with his vision for Britain, but how the new prime minister makes it a reality remains something of a mystery for businesses, lawmakers and even his most vocal supporters.
items.body:
[USN:L6N43M0R2 TEXT:"Andy Burnham"] has restored some hope to his governing Labour Party with his vision for Britain, but how the new prime minister makes it a reality remains something of a mystery for businesses, lawmakers and even his most vocal supporters.
At the Labour Party's annual conference in the northwestern English city of Liverpool, the mood was much more upbeat than the last two years of [USN:L8N41P1MT TEXT:"Keir Starmer"]'s administration but there were nagging questions. It remains unclear when Burnham will plot a detailed route and allocate the funds to become the "[USN:L1N43M05W TEXT:"circuit-breaker"]" for Britain's recently unstable politics.
After promising to ease cost-of-living pressures and to spur economic growth through reindustrialisation and devolving power to the regions, there is little detail on how Burnham will fund and implement his feel-good agenda in the near term, companies and lawmakers say. They say he is more focused on the future, specifically after the next national election, due in mid-2029.
Even his [USN:L1N45L05W TEXT:"first conference speech"] as prime minister, in which he offered an "honest conversation" on the deepest problems afflicting Britain and the trade-offs involved in tackling them, posed more questions than answers on immediate policy decisions.
Burnham himself concedes he is boxed in by Starmer's earlier election promises, limiting not only his room to raise funds for his more ambitious aims before the next national election, but also preventing him from bringing in his own agenda.
CONFERENCE LACKED DETAILED POLICIES, SAYS BUSINESS EXEC "The whole conference feels like it is in a haze of dope," said one business executive, speaking on condition of anonymity. "It is nice to be here. But it feels like everything is moving slowly."
"The frustrating thing is some big ideas are being thrown about, but we don't know enough about how they are going to work."
Companies, which paid about £6,000 ($7,925) to attend Labour's business day and the wider conference, and lawmakers, nervously eyeing opinion polls, want answers — how will the government cut energy costs, borrowing and welfare, and is there money to spend on defence, health and education before the next election.
Burnham has promised to set out a 10-year plan later in the year, and has pushed back one major commitment — [USN:L6N45J04E TEXT:"the reform of social care"] — saying he would only present proposals at the next election, due by mid-2029.
But after offering some short-term "breathing space" to Britons struggling with cost-of-living pressures, Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade has failed so far to offer, particularly to businesses, a blueprint of the government's investment strategy and its plans to deliver lower costs.
The scale of the problems facing Britain has created some sympathy for Burnham, the former mayor who had been in parliament just a month when he became prime minister in July, after Starmer resigned earlier than expected.
Alex Sobel, a Labour lawmaker, told Reuters Burnham had been dealt some of the trickiest challenges of any prime minister in modern history, including the rise of AI and wars in Iran and Ukraine pushing up Britain's energy prices.
"You can't say you have had three months, and everything should be sorted by now," he said.
POLL BOOST MIGHT QUICKLY DISAPPEAR, SAYS POLLSTER However, that understanding has its limits and the bounce in the opinion polls since Burnham took power could soon disappear.
John Curtice, Britain's best-known pollster, said Burnham's five-point bounce was very similar to that enjoyed by former Labour Prime Minister Gordon Brown and former Conservative Prime Minister Boris Johnson when they took on their roles mid-term.
Both lost their jobs about three years later.
"Things are better, but the party needs to do much more to win the next election," Curtice said.
That means supporting businesses still angered by the tax and wage increases brought in by Starmer, and offering a clear signal about which sectors will benefit from government spending so they can increase investment.
One attendee of Labour's business day on Monday said while the access to ministers was the best they had ever had, the real test would be the budget and the 10-year plan. They remain desperate for policy details.
But Burnham must also convince voters he can ease cost-of-living pressures such as energy bills over the long term, start a mass house-building programme and deliver higher defence spending and jobs, all without diverting spending on Britain's struggling public services, such as health.
Businesses and lawmakers hope for more clarity in finance minister John Healey's October 28 budget, although his conference speech suggesting it would be business as usual made some worried that he was not yet ready to grasp the nettle.
"The grit is going to come," said Claire Ainsley, director of the Project on Center-Left Renewal at the Progressive Policy Institute and a former Starmer adviser.
"The things that it's going to take to reboot the economy are not necessarily the things that Labour members want to do."
At least eight Labour lawmakers canvassed by Reuters said that if the government fails to deliver, that could hand power to the populist Reform UK party, led by Brexit campaigner Nigel Farage.
The removal of Starmer for the more popular Burnham would have been all for nothing, one said.
"We have to deliver. We have no choice," said Labour lawmaker Chris Curtis. "That is why we have to be bold and come up with solutions to those challenges."

items.title: Preso em um inferno após ataque russo, cientista ucraniano teve que escalar para se salvar
items.author: Daria Smetanko
items.creator: Daria Smetanko
items.summary: Ihor Malchevsky concentrou-se exclusivamente em sua família enquanto espreitava pela beirada da janela de seu escritório no terceiro andar, com uma espessa fumaça preta subindo atrás de si após um drone russo se chocar contra o prédio histórico, incendiando-o.
items.body:
Ihor Malchevsky concentrou-se exclusivamente em sua família enquanto espreitava pela beirada da janela de seu escritório no terceiro andar, com uma espessa fumaça preta subindo atrás de si após um drone russo se chocar contra o prédio histórico, incendiando-o.
“Meus pensamentos estavam voltados para apenas uma coisa: como me salvar dessa situação”, disse o homem de 69 anos, vice-chefe de departamento da Academia Nacional de Ciências da Ucrânia, no centro de Kiev, atingida na segunda-feira.
Malchevsky concentrou-se em sua esposa, seus dois filhos adultos e seus sete netos. Seu medo de altura não o impediu de se equilibrar do lado de fora da janela para fugir da intensa fumaça e das chamas violentas.
Imagens de Malchevsky e de um colega presos no prédio em chamas, construído na era czarista, alimentaram uma nova onda de indignação diante da escalada dos ataques russos à capital ucraniana, Kiev, e a outras cidades.
Nas últimas semanas, Moscou ampliou seus ataques fatais para atingir a logística de consumo, empresas e data centers. A Ucrânia atacou infraestruturas de petróleo e de defesa na Rússia, assim como varejistas online.
O ataque de segunda-feira, que matou uma pessoa e feriu várias outras, foi mais um de uma série crescente de ataques diurnos ao centro de Kiev, utilizando drones a jato desenvolvidos pela Rússia para superar as defesas aéreas ucranianas.
CENAS CAÓTICAS Em entrevista à Reuters um dia depois do ataque, Malchevsky relembrou os momentos caóticos após o drone se chocar contra o edifício amarelo ornamentado, a poucos passos da Ópera Nacional e da embaixada alemã.
“Nos primeiros segundos você não entende nada -- depois a mente entra em ação e começa a analisar o que aconteceu”, disse em uma entrevista dele, nos arredores de Kiev.
Lá embaixo, sirenes e alarmes de carros soavam enquanto transeuntes gritavam e as chamas rugiam pelo prédio.
Após momentos tensos agarrado à lateral do prédio, enquanto dezenas de curiosos observavam prendendo a respiração, Malchevsky desceu cautelosamente por uma escada fornecida pelas equipes de resgate.
Praticamente ileso, o pacato Malchevsky chegou à calçada e se sentou, ainda atordoado, em um parque do outro lado da rua, onde bebeu água em grandes goles para aliviar os efeitos da fumaça na garganta.
Familiares correram para o local após Malchevsky ligar para eles.
Sua filha, Kateryna Moskaliuk, de 37 anos, relembrou o momento em que bateu os olhos em seu pai após o ataque, coberto de fuligem.
Ela sorriu aliviada, mas expressou consternação pelas inúmeras outras famílias ucranianas afetadas por mais de quatro anos de guerra.
“Para que serve tudo isso?”, perguntou Moskaliuk.
Os ucranianos esperam mais um inverno de ataques russos violentos à rede de energia do país, em meio à escassez de suprimentos essenciais para a defesa aérea.
Malchevsky -- cujos netos, brincando, o compararam ao “Homem-Aranha” depois de verem o vídeo no YouTube -- disse que a Ucrânia deve seguir lutando para enfraquecer a Rússia, apesar das tentativas de retomada das negociações de paz apoiadas pelos Estados Unidos.
Uma autoridade norte-americana afirmou nesta terça-feira que Kirill Dmitriev, o enviado do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, teve conversas “construtivas” com seus homólogos norte-americanos.
