items.title: ジェフリーズ、資産運用収入50%超減－株式トレーディングは過去最高
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米ジェフリーズ・フィナンシャル・グループが28日発表した6－8月（第3四半期）決算では、資産運用部門の収入が50%以上減少した。投資案件を巡る問題が重荷となっている。決算発表を受けて株価は下落した。

発表資料によると、資産運用部門の純収入は8560万ドル（約135億円）と、前年同期の約1億7700万ドルから減少した。傘下にあるルーカディア・アセット・マネジメントのポイント・ボニータ・ファンドを通じて投資していた米自動車部品メーカー、ファースト・ブランズ・グループと鉄鉱石商社ラディアント・ワールドへの投資が裏目に出ている。

ジェフリーズ株はニューヨーク時間午後4時57分（日本時間29日午前5時57分）時点の時間外取引で2.4%安の46ドル。

リチャード・ハンドラー最高経営責任者（CEO）とブライアン・フリードマン社長は発表資料で「事業の長期的な見通しには引き続き自信を持っている。昨秋にヒルデンの50%持ち分取得と資金拠出を発表した際の戦略に沿い、一部の既存ファンドへの資本配分を減らすことで事業基盤を再構築している」と説明した。

ジェフリーズは2025年、長年にわたり戦略的関係を築いてきたクレジット運用会社ヒルデン・ホールディングの50%持ち分取得で合意した。

資産運用部門の不振で、株式トレーディングと投資銀行部門がともに過去最高となった好業績もかすんだ。株式トレーディング収入は前年同期比29%増の6億2600万ドル。現物・電子取引に加え、ヘッジファンド向けプライムサービスが寄与した。

投資銀行部門の収入は17%増の13億ドル。アドバイザリー業務が25%、株式引受業務が69%それぞれ増加し、収入を後押しした。

ラディアント・ワールドにはここ数カ月、不正疑惑を巡り厳しい目が向けられている。ブルームバーグはこれまでに、ジェフリーズのラディアント・ワールド向けエクスポージャーを3億ドル未満と報じている。

items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： OpenAIは、安全性を巡る懸念を理由に次世代AIモデル「GPT-6.1 Astra（アストラ）」のリリースを中止した。安全性評価で現行バージョンと同等の性能を発揮できず、見送りを決めた。

OpenAIは28日、「限定されたスコープ（アクセス範囲）と権限内にとどまることや、実行した作業の種類をユーザーにどのように伝えるか」という点で、同社が期待したほど良好な結果が出なかったと安全システム責任者サーチ・ジェイン氏の説明を公表した。

大手AI開発会社が安全性を理由に新バージョンのリリースを断念するのは、極めて異例だ。業界では今夏を通じてAIシステムの暴走に関する報告が相次いだ。リリース中止は、AIエージェントの不正侵入などの不安が業界の急速な発展を脅かす最も明確な兆候の一つと言える。

米紙ウォールストリート・ジャーナル（WSJ）が先に報じたところでは、GPT-6.1 Astraは10月のリリースが当初予定されていた。OpenAIのジェイン氏は同紙とのインタビューで、GPT-6.1 Astraについて、従来モデルに比べ二つの領域で性能が後退し、安全にリリースする十分な信頼性を確保できなかったと語った。

同紙によれば、人間の意図から外れたAIの行動などを抑えることを目的としたアラインメント（制御・安全設計）に関連し、人間の意向にどの程度忠実か測定する試験で、GPT-6.1 Astraの成績は思わしくなかった。

ごまかしのレベルがより高く、実行した行為やしなかったことをユーザーに正直に伝えないケースがあったほか、許可を求めずにタスクを実行したり、安全でない可能性があっても外部のツールやサービスを利用しようとしたりするなど、スコープ認可からの逸脱も確認された。

OpenAIは、同社のAIエージェントが外部システムに侵入した一連のセキュリティーインシデントを相次ぎ公表し、AIを人間が制御できなくなるとの不安が一層高まる事態となっていた。先週25日には自律型AIシステムの一つが安全なテスト環境から抜け出し、インターネットに接続したと発表。最も高性能なモデルの訓練を一時停止する方針を明らかにした。

items.title: イラン当局者、米中間選挙前の合意に悲観的－米国との協議進展乏しく
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： イラン当局者は、11月の米中間選挙までに米国との敵対行為を終結させ、ホルムズ海峡を再開する合意に達することについて、非公式に悲観的な見方を示している。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。

関係者によると、イランと米国が先週、国連総会に合わせてニューヨークで行った協議ではほとんど進展がなかった。イランは11月3日の投票後に紛争が激化する可能性が高いとみているという。一部の関係者はイラン当局者から説明を受けた。機密性の高い内容だとして、関係者はいずれも匿名を条件に語った。

イラン当局者は一貫して、外交を追求する意思はあるものの、トランプ米大統領の政権が合意条件を順守するとは信頼していないと述べてきた。ホワイトハウスもイラン政府に対して同様の不信感を抱いており、トランプ氏はこれまで、中間選挙前に合意に達することができるか疑わしいとの見方を示している。

トランプ氏は28日、イランとの協議について記者団から問われ、米国の代表者が仲介者と接触していると説明した。協議内容については明らかにしなかった。

同氏は大統領執務室で記者団に「われわれは勝つ」と述べ、「私に言わせれば、どちらにしても決着する。かなり早く進むだろう」と語った。

機密性の高い協議だとして匿名を条件に語った米当局者1人によると、イランの核開発計画を巡る問題が解決されない限り、同国との合意はない。トランプ氏は、核問題で具体的な進展が得られることと引き換えに、対イラン制裁を緩和し、凍結資金を解放する用意があるという。

関係者1人によると、先週トランプ氏の特使ジャレッド・クシュナー、スティーブ・ウィトコフ両氏と会談したイランのアラグチ外相は、追加協議のため米国にとどまっている。協議は仲介者を通じて行われる。

イラン学生通信（ISNA）によると、アラグチ氏が参加する協議は現地時間28日午前に行われ、最近の提案を検討するとともに、現状について意見を交換する。米国の代表者は出席しないという。

items.title: 東京で住宅購入、過半数が「1、2年先」を希望－値上がり警戒、検討中の1000人調査
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 東京の住宅市場では、高止まりする物件価格と生活費の上昇が購入の足かせとなっている。ブルームバーグ・インテリジェンス（BI）の調査では、東京23区内で住宅購入を検討する人の過半数が購入時期を1、2年先と見込んでいると回答した。一方、約3分の2は今後1年間の値上がりを見込んでおり、購入を慎重に進めようとする姿勢と、価格の先高観が併存している。

9月28日公表のリポートによると、今後2年以内に住宅購入を予定する1000人のうち、54%が購入時期を1－2年以内と回答した。割合は2025年9月調査の59%、26年1月の56%から低下したものの、依然として半数を超えている。

1年以内の購入を予定している人のうち、3カ月以内を目指すと答えたのは11%、4－6カ月以内は15%、7－12カ月以内は17%で、いずれも前回の調査結果と比べて変化はほとんど見られなかった。

東京の住宅価格や生活費の高騰により、住宅購入を検討している人は決定に慎重になっている。当初の購入計画を延期または見合わせるとした人は38%と、1月の37%から小幅に増えた。予定通りとした人は31%、前倒しするとした人は30%だった。

延期や見合わせを決めた381人に理由を尋ねたところ、価格下落を待ちたいとの回答が21%、生活費の上昇が19%を占めた。景気見通しの悪化を挙げた割合は18%と、25年9月の12%、26年1月の13%から上昇。BIは、円安と原油高による輸入価格の上昇が、購入検討者に予算や返済余力の再点検を促す可能性があると分析した。

販売面にも逆風が見られる。リポートが引用した不動産経済研究所のデータでは、首都圏の新築マンション在庫戸数は8月末時点で6610戸と、前年同月比16%増加した。三井不動産の4－6月期の販売戸数は前年同期比31%減の797戸。一方、三菱地所のマンション販売戸数は5%増の483戸、住友不動産は横ばいの520戸だった。

items.author: CNA
items.summary: British police are investigating a suspected plot to attack RAF Fairford, a base used by US bombers, with five British men arrested and released on bail.

UK examines foreign state involvement in suspected airbase plot, releases suspects

British police are investigating a suspected plot to attack RAF Fairford, a base used by US bombers, with five British men arrested and released on bail.

British newspaper front pages reporting the police declaration of a major incident at RAF Fairford airbase in this illustration, Sep 28, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Melville)

FAST

FAIRFORD: British police said on Monday (Sep 28) they were investigating whether individuals acting for a foreign state were involved in an apparent plot to attack an airbase used by the United State s but said five suspects they had arrested would be released on bail.
The five men, all British nationals from London in their early 20s, were detained early on Sunday after police were alerted by a local farmer about three white vans driving towards RAF Fairford, a British base that houses US bombers that fly missions against Iran.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in July the base was a legitimate target.
Laurence Taylor, who heads Britain's counter-terrorism police, said the men, who had been arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and planning a terrorist act, would be released under stringent bail conditions on Monday.
INVESTIGATION IS NOT OVER

"To be very clear, this does not mean that the investigation is over," Taylor said in a state ment outside London police headquarters. "They absolutely remain under investigation as we explore multiple lines of enquiry."
US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House on Monday that the incident "might be" connected to Iran, adding that he would not have released the suspects on bail. "I wouldn't have done that," he said.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was a foreign actor involved, without providing evidence or specifying details.
"What happened, what almost happened, what could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation. It's one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor. I won't get into great detail about that yet," Rubio said on the Fox News network's Hannity program late on Monday.
A source familiar with the investigation had told Reuters that an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, although a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at as possibilities.
Iran's embassy in London had earlier said in a state ment it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations" that it was involved, which it said would fuel "Iranophobia propaganda" in Britain.
Taylor, who did not specifically refer to Iran, said he knew there was significant interest in whether the current geopolitical context had a bearing on this incident.
"Be assured, we are considering this from every possible angle, including that this may be actively committed by proxies or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly working on behalf of a foreign state ."

Armed police officers work on a road outside the perimeter of the RAF Fairford airbase, Gloucestershire, Britain, Sep 27, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

POLICE REMAIN AT SCENE Taylor said the three white vans had been subject to extensive examination, with the support of the military and forensic experts, and police still had "significant resources deployed at the scene".
Trump said on Sunday that the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, doubts were voiced in British media about the degree to which they had been under surveillance, given how close they had come to the base.
The source familiar with the investigation said the arrests were not "intelligence-led", although security had been heightened at the base, suggesting authorities were aware of an increased threat.
The farmer who alerted the police told reporters she had seen a group of "hooded and masked men" running into fields. The farmer, who has not been identified, said she believed it was her phone call to the 999 emergency hotline that foiled any plot and that she thought she had seen up to 10 people at the scene.
Defence minister Wes Streeting told the BBC the farmer had only a "partial picture" of the investigation, without providing further clarification.
"We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies," Streeting said.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a meeting of the government's emergency response committee.
TERRORISM THREAT SEVERE Britain raised its national terrorism threat level to its second-highest level in April after a series of antisemitic incidents in north London, meaning an attack is considered highly likely.
Police said they were investigating links with Iran to many of those incidents in which properties connected to the Jewish community or Iranian dissidents were targeted.
After the Fairford arrests, the US embassy issued a security alert saying US citizens should exercise caution and be "mindful of personal security". Security was stepped up at other US airbase s in Britain.
The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
In Fairford, police imposed a 400m cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes in the nearby village of Whelford.
"Thanks to the excellent work of the army's explosive ordnance disposal team, the scene is now safe, and the residents of Whelford will shortly be returning home," British interior minister Shabana Mahmood said.

Source: Reuters/fs

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's meeting with tech CEOs on artificial intelligence on Tuesday (Sep 28) will focus on finding a balance between innovation and oversight, Ho us e Speaker Mike Johnson s ai d, as the federal government seeks to define its role in the burgeoning tech nology.
"We do not need a moratorium. We do not need to jump in and hyper-regulate this, beca us e we'll lose the race to China," Johnson s ai d in an interview on Monday with Fox B us iness Network. "The innovation is important to continue, but we have to strike the right balance . That's what the conversation is going to be about."
Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Open AI 's Greg Brockman and Nvidia's Jensen Huang are among those who will attend Tuesday's meeting with Trump and Johnson, according to sources familiar with the matter. Other possible attendees include Google CEO Sundar Pich ai and Spacex AI executive Elon M us k.
The White Ho us e meeting comes as leading AI companies are calling for slowing development of increasingly capable AI systems , warning of the risks to humanity and appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful tech nology.

Trump has downplayed concerns over the mis us e of artificial intelligence harming people as he stressed the importance of maintaining America's competitive edge over China. He says the US already has guardr ai ls in place for the powerful tech nology, including at the Department of J us tice.
Johnson s ai d the US should be mindful of safety but not stymie the tech nology's development. "I think there may be a role for the DOJ if things go awry. But what we need before we get to that stage is transparency, and we need some oversight," he s ai d on "Mornings with Fox B us iness."
Lawmakers in both parties have questioned Trump's hands-off approach even as the tech nology r ai ses fears about safety, job losses and the concentration of power among a handful of tech companies.
Ho us e Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries s ai d AI ind us try leaders were pleading for some government action and Congress has a responsibility to protect the American people.
"So, when it comes to AI safety, it cert ai nly seems to me that we need to actually lean in boldly and responsibly - now," Jeffries told CNBC on Monday.
The president had dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday.
Anthropic and its rivals have called for slowing AI development. These include Open AI , Google’s DeepMind, Microsoft and x AI .

US, Iran officials separately talk with mediators in latest bid to end war Any further talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly

Iran's seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars' worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports | Photo: Bloombe

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 29 2026 | 7:58 AM IST

Listen to This Article

US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part of a renewed effort to end seven months of war, according to officials of both countries.
  Any further talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters.
  The war began in late February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran, killing thousands of people over seven months and shocking global markets as vital waterways for oil remained choked. The US and Iran have twice previously agreed to ceasefires in mediated peace talks, in April and June. Those agreements quickly unraveled.
 

  Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, who remained in New York after attending the General Assembly, said Iran expected to receive the US response to its latest ceasefire proposals and its conditions for restoring passage of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state news agency IRNA.
  "If the Americans claim they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we have presented that solution," Araqchi said.
Also Read

US officials separately spoke with mediators on Monday, US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House, without giving further details.
Trump has flagged further talks this week Iran's seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars' worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports.

  Iran would then allow the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for oil tankers, and the two sides would also resume talks on Iran's nuclear program and Trump's wish to seize or eliminate its highly enriched uranium.
  Trump said on Saturday he had rejected Iran's proposal, saying Iran wanted a swift agreement because of the crippling economic pressure it is under. However, he also told Axios on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in further talks this week.
  Araqchi said on Sunday that mediators had not formally conveyed a US rejection, and that Iran was awaiting Washington's definitive position before deciding its next steps.

  "Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," he said on Sunday, adding that only a negotiated solution could resolve the impasse. 

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: 米ジャンク債に需給悪化の兆し、投資家消化しきれず－ゴールドマン
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ゴールドマン・サックス・グループのチーフ・クレジット・ストラテジスト、アマンダ・ライナム氏は28日、米国のハイイールド債市場で、急増した社債の発行を投資家が吸収しきれなくなり始め、リスクプレミアムが5カ月ぶりの高水準に上昇していると指摘した。

ライナム氏は、ブルームバーグテレビジョンで「市場は、夏の初めに投資適格債市場で見られたのと同じような、一時的な需給悪化に備えている。ハイイールド債でもそれが起きている」と語った。

ソフトバンクグループによる100億ドル（約1兆5700億円）の起債など、大型のジャンク債発行が相次いだことで、9月の社債発行額は385億1000万ドルに達し、ハイイールド債市場では今年最も発行が活発な月となった。一方、パラマウント・スカイダンスは今週、投資適格債とハイイールド債で444億ドルを調達する計画だ。

ライナム氏によると、相次ぐ起債に加え、今年後半も多くの案件が予定されていることや債券利回りの上昇が、社債スプレッドへの上昇圧力となっている。ブルームバーグの指数データによると、ジャンク債と米国債の利回り差（スプレッド）は、25日終値時点で12ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）拡大して294bpと、4月以来の高水準に達した。

信用力が最も低い層であるCCC格社債の平均スプレッドは968bpで、2023年11月以来の高水準となった。

債券利回りの上昇により、社債は利回りを重視する投資家にとって、魅力的な投資先となっているが、ゴールドマンは、金利上昇でクレジットスプレッドが拡大するリスクを警戒している。

ライナム氏によると、ゴールドマンの集計では、今年これまでに債券市場でAI関連の取り組みに伴う発行額が約6000億ドルという「極めて驚異的な数字」に達している。このうちハイパースケーラー関連は約40%にとどまり、AI関連の資金調達がいかに幅広く広がっているかが示された。

items.title: 【欧州市況】債券下落、原油と天然ガス価格上昇受け－株は横ばい
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 28日の欧州債券市場は、原油と天然ガス価格の上昇によりインフレ懸念が増したことで、下落した。

ドイツ30年債利回りは一時6ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）近く上昇して3.97%と、9日以来の大幅上昇となった。

ラガルド欧州中央銀行（ECB）総裁が、前回の政策委員会会合以降の債券利回り上昇は成長とインフレを鈍化させると述べたことを受け、短期金融市場では、今後5カ月間の利上げ観測が後退した。

英国債も売られ、2年債利回りは一時10bp上昇して4.94%となった。ヒーリー英財務相が、労働党大会での演説で財政規律を堅持する考えを表明したものの、市場の反応は限定的だった。

欧州株はほぼ横ばいだった。米10年債利回りが5.25%を上回ったことを受け、それまでの上げを失った。

ストックス欧州600指数は、ほぼ変わらずで取引を終えた。英住宅建設会社のテイラー・ウィンピー、ベルウェイ、パーシモン、バラット・レッドロウがいずれも10%超上昇した。英政府が初めて住宅を購入する人を対象とする新たな融資制度を発表し、JPモルガン・チェースのアナリストが「状況を一変させる」可能性があると評したことが材料となった。

世界的に債券利回りが上昇する中、欧州株は今月、5カ月続いた上昇に終止符を打つ可能性がある。

原題：30Y Bunds Suffer Worst Day Since Sept. 9: End-of-Day Curves、European Stocks Steady as Bond Rout Offsets UK Homebuilder Gains（抜粋）

items.title: 英中銀ラムズデン副総裁、インフレ上振れ圧力強まれば利上げも
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のラムズデン副総裁は、インフレの「上振れ圧力」が引き続き強まれば、利上げに踏み切る用意があると述べた。

ラムズデン氏は28日にロンドンで行った講演で、エネルギー価格の上昇が賃金と物価の上昇の連鎖を引き起こす恐れがあるとの見方を示した。ブリーデン、ロンバルデリ両副総裁も先週、同様の懸念を示していた。

金融政策委員会（MPC）は今月、6対3で政策金利を3.75%に据え置くことを決めたが、インフレ率は4%前後でピークに達するとの見通しを示した。これは英中銀の従来予想を大幅に上回り、同行が対応を迫られる水準となる。投資家らは11月の英中銀会合で0.25ポイントの利上げを見込んでいる。

ラムズデン氏は、イラン戦争に伴うエネルギーコストの上昇が物価に及ぼすリスクを引き続き注視していると説明。国内の食品価格への二次的な影響を示す兆候や、近く公表される企業の賃上げ計画に関する調査を見極める考えを示した。

同氏は「インフレ見通しへの上振れ圧力がさらに強まるようであれば、政策金利を引き上げる根拠となり得る」と発言。「インフレ見通しを巡るリスクは、外部・国内の要因ともに、上振れ方向に一段と傾いている」と述べた。

その一方で、英中銀の現在の政策スタンスはすでに引き締め的だとも強調。イラン戦争がなければ、「今ごろまでに少なくとも2回の利下げが行われ、政策金利は現在より少なくとも0.5%低い水準になっていたはずだ」と語った。

原題：BOE’s Ramsden Joins Warnings That Rates May Have to Rise

items.title: ECBラガルド総裁、利回り上昇で成長鈍化・インフレ波及を抑制
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 欧州中央銀行（ECB）のラガルド総裁は、債券利回りの上昇が景気拡大を抑えるとともに、エネルギーコスト上昇がインフレに波及するのを限定するとの見方を示した。

ラガルド氏は28日、欧州議会の公聴会で「成長は底堅さを維持しているものの、前回会合以降、長期金利は大幅に上昇した。これにより成長は鈍化し、インフレへの波及も9月の見通しで予想した以上に抑えられるだろう」と述べた。

これまでのところ二次的な影響は見られておらず、ECBは「インフレを抑制するため、必要に応じて慎重に対応すべきだ」と、同氏は語った。

ECB当局者は、インフレを抑制し、エネルギー価格の上昇が幅広い物価や賃上げ要求に波及するのを防ぐため、追加利上げの必要性を検討している。

中東での紛争に加え、ECB当局者は世界的な債券売りにも対応を迫られている。これは、財政が逼迫（ひっぱく）している一部のユーロ圏加盟国にとって特に懸念材料となっている。

原題：ECB’s Lagarde Says Higher Yields to Slow Growth and Inflation

items.title: メタ、法人向けのAI事業に参入－責任者にモンゴDBのCEOを起用
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米メタ・プラットフォームズは、法人顧客向けの新たなAIプラットフォームを率いる責任者に、データベースソフトウエアを手掛けるモンゴDBの社長兼最高経営責任者（CEO）を起用した。マーク・ザッカーバーグCEOは同事業を「次の主要な柱」と位置付けている。

チランタン・CJ・デサイ氏がチーフ・エンタープライズ・プラットフォーム・オフィサーに就任し、法人向けの新たなAIサービスを統括すると、ザッカーバーグ氏が28日、X（旧ツイッター）への投稿で明らかにした。

新事業「メタ・エンタープライズ・プラットフォーム」は、企業がAIを活用して成長し、新たな形で変革を遂げるのを支援する。ザッカーバーグ氏は、高度なモデルやAIエージェント、AIインフラに加え、「多くの企業と長年緊密に協力してきた経験」など、メタの強みを生かすと説明した。

モンゴDB株は一時27%安の300.00ドルまで急落した。マイクロソフトやセールスフォース、サービスナウなど企業向けソフトウエア株も下落。メタ株も4.8%安で終えた。

モンゴDBは28日、取締役会がデブ・イティチェリア氏を暫定社長兼CEOに復帰させたと発表した。同氏は2014年から2025年まで両職を務めていた。取締役会は、デサイ氏の正式な後任選びに着手した。

メタは今年、AI向け計算能力やAIモデルへのアクセスを販売するクラウドインフラ事業の計画策定に着手した。AI戦略を推進する中で、新たな収益源の開拓を進めていることが背景にある。

新設する法人向け事業は、スーパーインテリジェンス（超知能）を個人や企業、それらを支える開発者が利用できるようにするというザッカーバーグ氏が最終的に目指す構想の一環でもある。

また、マイクロソフト、アルファベット傘下グーグル、アマゾン・ウェブ・サービス（AWS）といった大手の法人向けサービスに加え、オープンAIやアンソロピックとも、より直接的に競合する体制を整えることになる。

モンゴDBは28日、取締役会がデブ・イティチェリア氏を暫定社長兼CEOに復帰させたと発表した。同氏は2014年から2025年まで両職を務めていた。取締役会は、デサイ氏の正式な後任選びに着手した。

items.title: スペースX「スターシップ」､初の軌道到達－改良型衛星を実運用へ
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 宇宙技術開発大手、米スペースXの巨大ロケット「スターシップ」は現地時間28日朝、初めて軌道に到達した。上昇中にエンジン1基が故障し、一時はミッション遂行が危ぶまれたものの、同計画にとって節目となる成果を達成した。

スターシップは現地時間午前7時49分、テキサス州南部のスターベース発射施設から打ち上げられた。ロケットには同社の改良型スターリンク衛星26基が搭載されており、スペースXはこれらを全て軌道上に展開したと発表した。

スペースXの広報担当者ダン・フオット氏はライブストリームで、展開された衛星26基が既存のスターリンク・ネットワークとの接続に成功したと述べた。

スターシップは打ち上げから約35分後に衛星の展開を開始した。一方、当初約10時間を予定していた飛行は早めに終了した。エンジン故障を受けた判断とみられる。スターシップは打ち上げから約3時間後、ハワイ近海の太平洋に着水した。

米株式市場でスペースXは乱高下。一時は1.4%上昇したが、最終的には2.2%安の145.47ドルで引けた。

スターシップが宇宙に向けて上昇する途中、6基あるラプターエンジンのうち1基が予定より早く停止したため、スペースXのエンジニアチームは軌道投入の試みを一時中止した。しかし、データを確認した後、チームは試みを再開し、スターシップのラプターエンジン1基を燃焼させ、機体を初めて軌道に投入した。

飛行開始から約3時間後、スターシップは軌道を離れて大気圏に再突入。時速2万6900キロを超える速度に達した後、ハワイ近海で制御された状態で海面に突入し、その後爆発した。

今回のスターシップ試験飛行は14回目で、スペースXにとって重要な節目となる。これまでの打ち上げはいずれも、安全性を最大限確保するため、意図的に軌道到達の手前にとどめていた。米規制当局は今回、スペースXがスターシップを次の段階へ進めることを承認し、同社が機体を安全に軌道速度まで加速させ、制御された形で地球へ帰還させられると判断した。

items.title: スペースX「スターシップ」､初の軌道投入に成功－商用化へ前進
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 宇宙技術開発大手、米スペースXの巨大ロケット「スターシップ」は現地時間28日朝、初めて軌道に到達した。上昇中にエンジン1基が故障し、一時はミッション遂行が危ぶまれたものの、同計画にとって節目となる成果を達成した。

スターシップは現地時間午前7時49分、テキサス州南部のスターベース発射施設から打ち上げられた。今回の試験飛行は約10時間に及ぶ可能性がある。ロケットには同社の改良型スターリンク衛星26基が搭載されており、スペースXはこれらを軌道上に展開し、既存の宇宙インターネット網を強化する計画だ。

スターシップは打ち上げから約35分後に衛星の展開を開始した。飛行開始から約1時間後、衛星26基すべての展開に成功したと、スペースXが明らかにした。

米株式市場でスペースXは乱高下。一時は1.4%上昇したが、ニューヨーク時間午前10時21分現在は0.9%安で推移している。

スターシップが宇宙に向けて上昇する途中、6基あるラプターエンジンのうち1基が予定より早く停止したため、スペースXのエンジニアチームは軌道投入の試みを一時中止した。しかし、データを確認した後、チームは試みを再開し、スターシップのラプターエンジン1基を燃焼させ、機体を初めて軌道に投入した。

今回のスターシップ試験飛行は14回目で、スペースXにとって重要な節目となる。これまでの打ち上げはいずれも、安全性を最大限確保するため、意図的に軌道到達の手前にとどめていた。米規制当局は今回、スペースXがスターシップを次の段階へ進めることを承認し、同社が機体を安全に軌道速度まで加速させ、制御された形で地球へ帰還させられると判断した。

今回のミッションが成功すれば、さらに多くの軌道飛行への道が開かれる可能性がある。スペースXはすでに1万1000基を超える衛星からなるネットワークを展開しており、今回の投入で改良型スターリンク衛星「V3」がこれに加わる。スターシップは過去の打ち上げでもV3衛星を展開したが、これらは最終的に計画通り地球の大気圏で燃え尽きた。

items.title: North America is building rare earth plants faster than it is building rare earth engineers
items.author: Frik Els
items.creator: Frik Els
items.summary: Engineering degrees output is less than half the roughly 600 a year implied by DOE's estimate of need, and about a 15th of China's.
items.body:
North America is building rare earth plants faster than it is building rare earth engineers

Frik Els | September 25, 2026 | 2:40 pm
Careers   Critical Minerals   Education   News   Africa   Asia   Australia   Canada   China   Europe   Latin America   USA   Copper   Rare Earth  

Colorado School of Mines at sunset. ( Image: Connor Beekman )

On August 7, as US President Donald Trump hosted mining executives at a roundtable in Washington, representatives of all 14 accredited US mining schools attended a parallel Department of Energy workforce event . They left with the first serious federal funding for mining education in a generation, more than $180 million in total , part of a package of deals the White House put at more than $2 billion and Bloomberg tallied at $3 billion .

The biggest slice is a new DOE programme called PROSPECT (Providing Opportunities for Specialized Education in Critical Technologies), worth up to $100 million and aimed at doubling the number of graduates with mining, minerals and supply chain credentials within two years. DOE puts the country’s need at about 6,000 new mining engineers over the next decade.

The Department of War proposed another $81.3 million for three schools, with Colorado School of Mines in line for $32.7 million for a critical minerals innovation and commercialization hub in Golden, South Dakota Mines received $25 million for a scholars consortium with the University of Kentucky and Missouri S&T, and Johns Hopkins got $23.6 million for a recycling hub.

The PROSPECT funding notice is, however, “subject to availability of appropriated funds,” and Congress has yet to pass a single FY2027 spending bill, leaving the government on a stopgap that runs out on December 11.

The Department of War awards are also still listed as proposed. The only money moving so far is a $16 million PROSPECT Planning Prize  launched on September 14, which offers up to $1 million per school for plans to grow credential output within two years. Applications close on October 5. A GEM Consulting study found that public capital in mining increasingly comes with workforce conditions attached  and singled out the $180 million education line as money that “could ease workforce shortages affecting multiple projects.” Measured against the more than $10 billion already committed to US rare earths and magnets by Bloomberg’s count, the people side of the ledger is getting less than two cents on the dollar.

The NDAA provision is stuck in the Senate

The legislative route that put mining schools on the defence agenda this summer has gone nowhere since the House passed the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act by 216 votes to 212 on July 22. The bill authorises about $1.14 trillion in discretionary defence spending and carries the surviving core of Rep. Burgess Owens’ Mining Schools Act, now Section 1883 of the text passed by the House (numbered 1853 in the committee mark and in Owens’ own press release).

Section 1883 directs the Department of War to use Defense Production Act authorities to support workforce development in the mining, processing, refining and recycling of critical minerals through university partnerships, scholarships, tuition assistance and on the job learning. It also orders an assessment of whether certain awards should be conditioned on a company’s participation, which would make training a term of the contract.

The section authorises no money, and it is not the Energy Department grant programme with an advisory board that Owens’ release describes. That programme exists only in the standalone bill, H.R.2457, which has not had a markup since it was referred to the House Natural Resources Committee in March 2025. The Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration has been pushing a version of the bill since at least 2022 , when the number of accredited programmes had already fallen from 25 in the early 1980s to 14.

The Senate has neither taken up the House bill nor passed its own since a July 14 cloture vote on the motion to proceed to S.4784 failed 50 to 46, with Democrats objecting to the Iran war and the size of the bill. We could find no equivalent workforce section in the Senate text, and no conference has been convened. Congress has passed an NDAA every year for more than six decades, usually in the final weeks of December, which points to a vote after the November 3 midterms. In the meantime, the August package, which runs on existing DOE and Department of War authorities, has overtaken the bill.

Other measures announced earlier in the year have moved only on paper, including a May 29 presidential memorandum that approved critical position pay of up to $400,000 for as many as 400 federal roles recruiting investment and engineering talent, and the Office of Personnel Management turned it into a final rule on August 26 , but no hires under the authority have been reported. The Critical Mineral Mining Education Act (H.R.7021 and S.3612), which would fund a $10 million a year mining Fulbright through the State Department, has not moved since January.

The National Science Foundation’s Critical Materials Crossroads Engine , led by the University of Missouri Kansas City and selected in July for up to $160 million over 10 years, held its launch  at Kansas City’s Union Station on August 21. Only $15 million is committed for the first two years, with the remaining $145 million tied to milestone reviews. The launch materials list rare earth elements among the target materials alongside nickel, cobalt, lithium, graphite and gallium, but no rare earth separation track has been named.

A pipeline that shrank for decades

Only 14 US universities offer accredited mining engineering degrees, namely Alaska Fairbanks, Arizona, Colorado School of Mines, Kentucky, Michigan Tech, Missouri S&T, Montana Tech, Nevada (Reno), New Mexico Tech, Penn State, South Dakota Mines, Utah, Virginia Tech and West Virginia. Twelve universities, among them Berkeley, Columbia, Ohio State and Texas A&M, have closed mining programmes since 1985. US schools awarded 700 bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mining in 1981, a level never reached again, and according to SME mining engineering enrolment fell from nearly 1,500 in 2015 to fewer than 600 in 2023.

Estimates of how many graduates the system produces vary with the source, as South Dakota Mines says fewer than 170 mining engineers a year, the National Mining Association says about 200, and Reuters counted just over 200 undergraduate mining and metallurgical degrees in 2023. Federal completions data compiled by Data USA show 285 mining and mineral engineering degrees at all levels in 2024, down 5%, with Colorado School of Mines (60), Missouri S&T (46) and Arizona (24) accounting for nearly half.

On any of those counts, output is less than half the roughly 600 a year implied by DOE’s estimate of need, and Bloomberg puts it at about a fifteenth of China’s . Doubling output, which is PROSPECT’s goal, would roughly close that gap, although PROSPECT counts credentials and not only four year degrees.

Colorado School of Mines warned of a “grey tsunami”  three years ago, when it put the number of US mining workers expected to retire by 2029 at 221,000, more than half the workforce. The estimate, which goes back to a 2014 SME briefing and was restated this summer as “within three years” , remains the only national figure available, and every measurable trend since has pointed the same way. US mining employment fell 20.4% over a decade , 71% of mining leaders surveyed by McKinsey said the talent shortage is already blocking production targets , and only 11% of young people say they would likely work in mining while 70% say they probably or definitely would not .

Juniors feel the squeeze most, with junior geologists now charging $500 to $600 a day , rates that four years ago belonged to senior geologists. US projects already take more than 30 years to move from discovery to production, and a shrinking pool of experienced technical workers  is slowing the engineering studies that come before a mine is built.

Flynn says the money goes to the wrong end of the chain

In July, retired Gen. Charles Flynn, former commander of US Army Pacific, argued that the federal rare earth buildout was missing the mark . About 90% of the raw material mined domestically still goes abroad for processing, nearly half the mining workforce reaches retirement age by 2029, and federal funding goes mostly to large producers while bypassing junior miners, their service providers and training. A $200 million grant to a single company, he noted, still leaves an 18 month gap before offtake begins.

“The country needs to think in terms of industrial systems and not just a collection of announcements and grants,” Flynn said.

Two months later the August package has answered his call for training money but done nothing for juniors, as the Office of Strategic Capital loans announced the same day went to Niron Magnetics , Sunrise Energy Metals  and Sila, all companies past the exploration stage. His other proposal, modular processing plants on military land, is already under way, with four companies building on army bases  and $725 million going to Energy Fuels and $500 million to Phoenix Tailings. The Pentagon has spent about $1 billion on rare earths since 2020  and expects its own magnet needs to reach about 10,000 tonnes a year by 2030.

From January 1, 2027, US defence contractors may no longer use Chinese magnets, a rule that applies to a country that used about 48,000 tonnes of magnets in 2025 against 300 tonnes of domestic supply . Even US-subsidised output is still being routed east  because the domestic separation and metallisation steps needed to consume it have yet to be built.

New plants will need people to run them

USA Rare Earth broke ground on September 9  on a $1.2 billion magnet plant in Blacksburg, South Carolina, with 6,400 tonnes a year of sintered NdFeB capacity, about 490 jobs and commissioning from 2028. The workforce line in the announcement was $250,000 for Spartanburg Community College’s new SPARK Center, roughly 0.02% of the capital cost, at a company that has lined up $1.6 billion in federal support . MP Materials says its $1.25 billion magnet campus in Texas , pitched at more than 1,500 jobs, is now “officially vertical.”

Energy Fuels began building its $104 million White Mesa heavy rare earth expansion  in Utah on July 29, with terbium and dysprosium circuits due by the end of 2027, while its $1.9 billion purchase of German magnet maker VAC, which employs more than 1,000 people in Hanau, still awaits approval from Berlin . Buying a trained magnet workforce is one way to get one. Vulcan Elements this week won a US Army contract to supply magnets for drones , its tenth with the Department of War, from a North Carolina plant with 10,000 tonnes a year of planned capacity and about 1,000 jobs. Cyclic Materials opened a 25,000 tonne a year recycling plant  in Mesa, Arizona, 17 months after announcing it, employing “dozens” of skilled workers.

Building a plant does not guarantee it will perform, as Serra Verde in Brazil  has shown with recoveries of 20% to 30% during ramp up against about 80% planned. The operation, which USA Rare Earth absorbed this month, has both the ore and the equipment, and its troubles point to the kind of operating experience China exports least willingly. EnerVenue cited much the same thing this week when it dropped a $264 million Kentucky battery plant for China , pointing to the “density of hydraulics, pneumatics and automation specialists” there.

MP Materials sued USA Rare Earth in May , accusing its rival of a pattern of recruiting MP employees to misappropriate trade secrets on magnet production, a sign of how scarce that experience already is outside China.

China treats rare earth expertise as a strategic asset

By Reuters’ count, at least 11 Chinese universities and technical colleges run dedicated rare earth degree programmes , enrolling more than 500 students a year and supported by more than 40 specialist laboratories, while no comparable undergraduate degree exists anywhere else. China’s Ministry of Education added a Rare Earth Materials Science and Engineering major to the national undergraduate catalogue in 2024, first approved at Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology in Baotou, 150km from the world’s largest rare earth mine.

Chinese financial media reported in June that Jiangxi University of Science and Technology in Ganzhou had been approved for a second major, Rare Earth Science and Engineering, and this term the university started an innovation class in the subject led by Li Chaozhong, dean of its rare earth school. “In China, I used to hire kids right out of university and they’re immediately productive. Anywhere else I need to train them for three years,” Constantine Karayannopoulos, former chief executive of Neo Performance Materials, told Reuters.

Reuters reported last October that there are only a couple of dozen experts in rare earth separation and refining in the US, Europe and Japan combined, compared with thousands in China , and that Beijing had started to catalogue its experts to make sure they do not travel abroad. China has long banned the export of rare earth extraction and separation technology and added magnet making technology to the list in December 2023 .

On September 15, State Council Decree No. 841 took effect, allowing authorities to bar Chinese citizens from leaving the country  if they breach export control or technology trade rules, or if they “may endanger” national industrial or technological security. The decree sets no time limit on such bans and allows notice to be withheld on national security grounds. It does not name rare earths, but Chinese commentators told Asia Times  it is aimed at sectors where Beijing already restricts exports, rare earths among them.

China’s magnet shipments to the US fell 21% in August to 512 tonnes , and some US buyers have waited more than six months for export licences . US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday that the trade truce, which includes the suspension of China’s October 2025 rare earth controls, would be extended by two months to January 10  as Xi Jinping began a state visit to Washington, although Beijing had yet to confirm the extension. JL Mag, the world’s largest magnet maker, is meanwhile targeting 60,000 tonnes a year of capacity by 2028 , against MP’s planned total of about 10,000 tonnes.

The three years of training Karayannopoulos describes matter because MP’s Texas campus and USA Rare Earth’s South Carolina plant both commission in 2028, while a student who started a US mining degree this month graduates in 2030.

Allies are short of engineers too

The usual answer, that the US can draw on Australian and Canadian graduates, does not survive a look at those countries’ enrolment data. In Australia, first year mining engineering enrolments fell from 267 in 2012 to 34 in 2018, and at UNSW from 120 in 2014 to six in 2018. Adelaide’s undergraduate degree is gone, Monash no longer offers one, and geoscience degree completions fell 40% over eight years , according to the Australian Geoscience Council.

The Minerals Council of Australia expects nearly half the country’s mining engineers to retire within the decade, and Canberra’s answer has been migration rather than education, with a skilled migration plan released on September 17 that prioritises engineers, geologists and metallurgists.

Canada has the most rigorous forecast, with the Mining Industry Human Resources Council’s June outlook putting the cumulative hiring requirement from 2026 to 2035 at 246,422 workers against a gap of 65,712, and acute shortages possible as early as 2027. Mining engineering enrolment peaked at 1,431 in 2014 and was down to 809 by 2022, yet seat utilisation averaged just 56% between 2021 and 2024, which means the places exist but the students do not.

Dalhousie closed its programme in 2024, while Saint Mary’s in Halifax expected a first resource engineering cohort of 20 to 25 students this autumn. Ottawa is relying on a C$81 million workforce alliance  and scholarships, and the Young Mining Professionals scholarship fund grew by a third this year . The updated Critical Minerals Strategy is still pending.

Britain had five mining schools turning out more than 300 graduates a year in 1990 , but Camborne School of Mines paused the country’s last undergraduate mining degree in 2020 and relaunched it only in 2025/26 , and the UK opened a £25 million critical minerals fund in August  that includes a magnet hub with a skills element. In Germany, RWTH Aachen closed its MSc in Mineral Resources Engineering to new entrants from 2024/25, although TU Bergakademie Freiberg is going the other way with a new raw materials bachelor’s from 2027/28. The EU’s Raw Materials Academy aims to train 100,000 learners by 2030 rather than grant degrees, and the Critical Raw Materials Act contains no skills article.

Where the top schools are

The 2026 edition of the QS subject ranking for mineral and mining engineering, published in March and current until the 2027 tables arrive next spring, puts Colorado School of Mines on top with an overall score of 95.8, more than 11 points clear of McGill in second place, while the rest of the top 30 fall within a band of about six points. MINING.COM last ran the list in 2022 , when Curtin and Queensland sat second and third.

Source: QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. Chart: MINING.COM

The US, Australia and Canada hold 17 of the top 30 places between them, and all three have seen enrolment fall hard. China places a single institution, China University of Mining and Technology at No. 29, with the lowest employer reputation score in the table, a reminder that QS measures academic and employer reputation among a largely Western survey panel rather than graduate numbers or industrial relevance.

Missouri S&T produced the second most US mining engineering degrees in 2024 and does not appear in the top 30, while Imperial College London scores a perfect 100 on employer reputation at No. 8 even though its mining department no longer exists under its own name. Russia’s St Petersburg Mining University sits at No. 11, ahead of Toronto, Virginia Tech and Arizona.

Where enrolment is growing

Colorado School of Mines says undergraduate mining engineering enrolment has doubled in three years, from 101 students in 2023 to about 183 by May, and this autumn it launched a minor in mineral processing and extractive metallurgy aimed at critical minerals recovery. DOE’s latest $10 million round of critical minerals research funding  went partly to Mines and the University of Arizona, where the MiningWerx pilot processing hub has $3.85 million in federal and state money. The University of Texas at El Paso is recruiting its first mining engineering class for autumn 2027 with $52 million from industry and the state, targeting 100 graduates a year, roughly a third of current national output.

Companies are also building pipelines of their own, and Neo Performance Materials’ partnership with Tallinn University of Technology in Estonia covers joint curricula and internships and is the only formal rare earth talent pipeline of its kind we have found outside China. USA Rare Earth’s demonstration plant in Wheat Ridge, Colorado runs a multistage solvent extraction circuit with 28 engineers, scientists and technicians on rotating shifts, a useful measure of what each new separation line needs in people. MP Materials grew from eight contractors in 2017 to 998 employees at the end of 2025, which shows a well funded operator can build a workforce, although juniors and service companies do not have MP’s balance sheet.

What comes next

The August 7 package is the first time Washington has put real money into mining education, and it deserves credit for that, but it amounts to $180 million, most of it proposed or awaiting appropriation, against more than $10 billion committed to plants. Section 1883 authorises no money and sits in a Senate that has not taken up the bill, and the Mining Schools Act has gone 18 months without a markup. The plants commission in 2028, this autumn’s freshmen graduate in 2030 and UTEP’s first class in 2031 at the earliest.

The next test comes on October 5, when applications close for the PROSPECT Planning Prize and the number of schools competing will show how much capacity exists to scale up. Congress then has until December 11, when the stopgap funding bill expires, to decide whether PROSPECT’s $100 million becomes real money, and on January 10 the extended truce covering China’s rare earth controls is due to run out.

items.title: A Lapel Pin Fuels Chinese Talk of a China-Russia-Iran Triangle
items.author: Rudy Lu
items.creator: Rudy Lu
items.summary: In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one another — for clues about relationships that official readouts rarely reveal.

A brief encounter between the foreign ministers of China, Russia and Iran at the BRICS summit has become the latest example.

Video from the sidelines of the summit in New Delhi showed Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi chatting and laughing with his Russian and Iranian counterparts Sergei Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi. At one point, Wang reached toward a pin on Araghchi’s jacket, prompting the Iranian foreign minister to laugh. 

Araghchi’s official Telegram channel later posted a close-up of the exchange , identifying the pin as an emblem depicting the map of Iran.

The moment quickly spread across Chinese social media, landing on the trending search list of Weibo, a Chinese social media platform often compared to X, under “Wang Yi helps the Iranian foreign minister straighten his pin” (#王毅帮伊朗外长整理胸针).

A wave of Chinese-language amplification followed.

Nationalist commentary account Rongping (戎评) described Iran as “holding the advantage” and in high spirits, with China and Russia sharing the mood. 

“Such a personal and warm interaction between the Chinese and Iranian foreign ministers sends a strong signal to the outside world: China-Iran relations have long gone beyond a simple exchange of interests, and the two sides share a high degree of familiarity and trust,” it wrote.

Another online commentary said the seemingly insignificant gesture reflected a shift in the international balance of power that would make the White House “deeply uncomfortable.”

“U.S. pressure is pushing the three sides closer together,” it said. “Washington can continue to pressure the three countries separately, but it will find it increasingly difficult to stop them from exchanging resources, coordinating positions and jointly seeking alternatives.”

It said Beijing could keep channels open to Gulf Arab countries, and Moscow could draw on its close strategic ties with Tehran. Working through BRICS, the three could help Iran break its diplomatic isolation and avert a complete rupture with the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states.

Those interpretations, however, largely reflect one strand of domestic online opinion that is sympathetic to Iran and distrustful of the United States. Beijing’s official posture has been more carefully calibrated, especially ahead of Xi Jinping’s scheduled Sept. 24 meeting with Trump in Washington.

Araghchi traveled to Beijing on Sep. 16 for talks with Wang Yi. The Chinese Foreign Ministry described Iran as a “comprehensive strategic partner” and said Beijing was prepared to help safeguard Tehran’s “legitimate rights and interests.” 

But much of Wang’s message focused on containing the conflict. He urged Iran and the United States to exercise restraint and return to negotiations, backed dialogue between Tehran and Gulf Arab governments, called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and warned against the fighting spreading toward Yemen and the Red Sea.

China’s balancing role was also evident when Saudi Arabia asked Beijing to press Iran to rein in the Houthis, Reuters reported, citing three Iranian sources . China then privately urged Tehran to use its influence over the Yemeni group, whose advances threatened Saudi oil exports and shipping through the Red Sea — a vital route for Chinese trade.

items.title: Rio Tinto to expand metals trading beyond own output
items.author: Cecilia Jamasmie
items.creator: Cecilia Jamasmie
items.summary: Mining giant targets third-party deals and derivatives as CEO Simon Trott seeks more value from its global asset base.
items.body:
Rio Tinto to expand metals trading beyond own output

Cecilia Jamasmie | September 24, 2026 | 4:46 am
Markets   Suppliers & Equipment   Top Companies   Asia   Australia   Europe   Aluminum   Copper   Iron Ore   Lithium  

Rio Tinto produces alumina as a core intermediate step in its vertically integrated aluminum business. ( Image courtesy of Rio Tinto. )

Rio Tinto (ASX, LON: RIO) plans to expand its metals trading business into third-party material and derivatives as chief executive Simon Trott seeks to squeeze more value from the world’s second-largest miner.

The initiative, Bloomberg reported , would mark a shift for Rio Tinto, which has historically focused on marketing its own production and operates a much smaller trading business than Glencore (LON: GLEN).

Glencore’s extensive trading network was one attraction during unsuccessful takeover talks between the companies over the past two years.

Rio Tinto does not intend to replicate standalone commodity trading houses, but is considering a significant expansion of its existing commercial business under chief commercial officer Bold Baatar, according to Bloomberg .

The push could give Rio greater flexibility to profit from regional supply imbalances and spare capacity across its global operations while broadening a commercial business that remains modest compared with major commodity traders.

Trading opportunities

Rio Tinto is considering more third-party trading in markets where its existing assets could provide an advantage. That includes alumina, where the company has surpluses in some regions and shortages in others.

In North America, its Kennecott operations have spare copper smelting capacity, creating opportunities to handle additional material. Rio Tinto could also trade copper cathode and related products such as sulphuric acid.

The commercial team currently has about 20 traders and could add several more as the company expands the operation.

The strategy fits with Trott’s broader overhaul of Rio Tinto since he became CEO last year . He has laid out plans to simplify the company, sell assets, cut costs and improve returns.

Rio Tinto is also in talks with Dutch multinational Vitol Group over a potential freight and logistics joint venture, another move that could reshape how the miner handles its global supply chain.

SK Hynix Is Eyeing Intel’s (INTC) Ohio Site. Why Micron (MU) Should Pay Attention

Habib Ur Rehman

SK Hynix is exploring something it has never done before: manufacturing memory chips in the United States.
Reuters reported on September 16 that the Korean memory giant is discussing several possibilities with Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ), including leasing part of Intel's long-delayed Ohio complex or forming a venture involving Intel and large cloud customers. SK Hynix said no specific plan has been finalized.
For Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU ), the talks matter because one of its strongest strategic advantages is being the major U.S.-based memory producer while AI has made DRAM and HBM increasingly scarce.

SK Hynix May Move Into Intel’s $100 Billion Ohio Fab. Micron Has a Reason to Watch SK Hynix Could Give Intel Another Path for Its Delayed Ohio Site Intel has committed enormous capital to Ohio, with the broader project potentially reaching around $100 billion over time. Delays have pushed planned production into the next decade. A tenant or joint-venture partner could therefore help Intel share the financial burden of developing the Ohio site rather than relying entirely on its own foundry demand to justify the buildout.

That is the bull case. The bear case is that exploratory talks are a long way from revenue. Bringing advanced Korean memory production to the U.S. could face cost problems, technology-transfer restrictions and objections from Seoul. Intel still needs its core manufacturing roadmap to work.
Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) sits on the other side of the equation. AI demand has pushed memory pricing and availability into a strong cycle, and Micron is already pursuing a large U.S. manufacturing expansion. More domestic manufacturing incentives and customer interest in secure supply support that plan.
A successful SK Hynix move could eventually erode part of Micron's U.S.-supply differentiation. U.S. cloud companies would gain another potential domestic supplier, while additional long-term memory capacity could eventually loosen the market that currently supports exceptional pricing.
Hedge funds loaded up on both chipmakers Insider Monkey tracked 138 hedge funds holding Intel in Q2, up sharply from 112 in Q1. AQR Capital Management held roughly 10.7 million shares after trimming its stake about 7%. Micron's count rose to 184 funds from 154, one of the stronger quarter-over-quarter increases among large semiconductor names. Coatue Management expanded its MU stake dramatically during the quarter.

Intel had about 152.2 million shares sold short as of August 31, roughly 3% of public float and 1.7 days to cover.
The talks do not rescue Intel's foundry strategy or weaken Micron overnight. They do show what AI scarcity is doing to the supply chain. Memory manufacturing is becoming strategic enough that SK Hynix is considering putting advanced capacity on American soil, and Intel's delayed Ohio project suddenly gives it a potentially valuable asset to negotiate with.

Story Continues
While we acknowledge the potential of INTC and MU as investments, we believe certain other AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
